definition_zh: 微观经济的；研究单个企业、住户或单个市场层面的
definition_en: relating to the choices of single firms, households or single markets rather than to the economy as a whole
core_image: 俯身看一间小店的账本：一位店主、一栏进货、一栏售价，视线只落在这一个柜台
scene: 一条街上开着许多小店，研究者却只盯住其中一家的账本。 The course begins with microeconomic choices made by a single household and a single firm.
sceneCN: 前半情境：一条街上许多小店，研究者只盯住其中一家的账本；句中的 microeconomic 指「以单个住户或单个企业为观察单位的」（第 1 个义项：研究单个主体而非全国总量）。图中可辨识物件：小店账本、价目牌、进货清单、算盘。

pos.zh: 微观经济的；单个主体层面的

derivatives.zh: 微观的；单个主体层面的

senses.title: Measured at the single unit
senses.definition: relating to one firm, one household or one producer rather than to totals for a whole country
senses.definitionCN: 与单个企业、单个住户或单个生产者相关，而非整个国家的总量
senses.example: Each microeconomic decision about hiring stays with the owner of the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 每一个关于雇人的微观经济决定都由店主自己作出。
senses.why: the prefix for 'small' is attached to economic, so the adjective marks the unit observed: one agent, not the aggregate.
senses.whyCN: 表示「小」的前缀加在「经济的」之上，这个形容词因而标出观察的单位：一个主体，而非总量。

senses.title: Concentrated on one market
senses.definition: relating to a single market in which one good or service is bought and sold
senses.definitionCN: 与买卖某一种商品或服务的单个市场相关
senses.example: The microeconomic question is why the price of one good rose.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的微观经济问题是：某一种商品的价格为何上涨。
senses.why: a single market is the smallest arena where supply meets demand, and the word marks that arena.
senses.whyCN: 单个市场是供给与需求相遇的最小场所，这个词标出的正是这个场所。

senses.title: Explaining individual choice
senses.definition: concerning the incentives and choices of individual buyers, workers or sellers
senses.definitionCN: 关于个体买方、劳动者或卖方的激励与选择
senses.example: Microeconomic reasoning explains why a consumer switches brands.
senses.exampleCN: 微观经济推理能解释消费者为何更换品牌。
senses.why: once the unit is a person or a firm, the question becomes what that unit chooses and why.
senses.whyCN: 一旦单位落到一个人或一家企业，问题就变成这个单位选择什么、为什么选择。

senses.title: Analysing one relation at a time
senses.titleCN: 一次只分析一重关系的
senses.definition: using partial analysis, in which one relationship is examined while everything else is held unchanged
senses.definitionCN: 采用局部分析，在其余条件不变时考察一重关系
senses.example: A microeconomic treatment isolates the effect of a single tax.
senses.exampleCN: 微观经济的处理方式把单一税种的影响单独分离出来。
senses.why: the method follows the unit: to see how one price responds, the analyst must keep the rest of the system still.
senses.whyCN: 方法跟单位走：要看清一个价格如何反应，分析者必须让系统的其余部分静止。

senses.title: Applied to a single industry
senses.definition: concerning the rules or performance of one industry or one sector rather than of the whole economy
senses.definitionCN: 关于某一个行业或某一个部门的规则或表现，而非整个经济
senses.example: Rules on one chain of stores are a microeconomic matter.
senses.exampleCN: 针对某一家连锁店的规则属于微观经济事项。
senses.why: an industry is a collection of units of the same kind, so policy aimed at it stays inside the word's scale.
senses.whyCN: 一个行业是同类单位的集合，针对它的政策仍在这个词的尺度之内。

senses.title: Built on disaggregated data
senses.titleCN: 基于分解到个体的数据的
senses.definition: based on data collected from separate units, such as individual households or individual plants
senses.definitionCN: 基于从各个独立单位收集的数据，如单个住户或单个工厂
senses.example: The survey provides microeconomic data on household spending.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查提供关于住户支出的微观经济数据。
senses.why: counting one unit at a time is what makes the smallest scale measurable, so the adjective also describes the data.
senses.whyCN: 逐个单位地数是使最小尺度可测量的方式，因此这个形容词也用来描述这类数据。

senses.title: Naming one branch of economics
senses.titleCN: 作为经济学的一个分支名称
senses.definition: naming the branch of economics that studies single units, as opposed to the branch that studies totals
senses.definitionCN: 命名研究单个单位的经济学分支，与研究对象为总量的分支相对
senses.example: The textbook turns from microeconomic foundations to national accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 这本教材从微观经济的基础转向国民账户。
senses.why: universities divided the subject by the size of its unit, and the adjective became the label of one half.
senses.whyCN: 大学按研究单位的大小划分这门学科，这个形容词便成了其中一半的名称。

senses.title: Applied beyond formal markets
senses.titleCN: 用于正式市场之外的微观分析
senses.definition: describing microeconomic reasoning applied to households, time use and other small-scale choices outside formal markets
senses.definitionCN: 描述把微观经济分析用于住户、时间分配等正式市场之外的小尺度选择
senses.example: Microeconomic reasoning explains how a household divides unpaid work between its members.
senses.exampleCN: 微观经济推理可以解释一户人家如何在成员之间分配无偿劳动。
senses.why: the unit of analysis stays the single household or person even when no market transaction is involved, so the adjective travels beyond price-setting.
senses.whyCN: 即使不涉及市场交易，分析单位仍是单户或单人，因此这个形容词能从定价扩展到别的选择。

intro.en: The adjective joins a Greek prefix meaning 'small' to economic, which descends from Greek oikonomikos by way of Latin oeconomicus. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个形容词把表示「小」的希腊前缀接在 economic 之前，而 economic 经拉丁 oeconomicus 来自希腊 oikonomikos。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mikros meant 'small, little'. The reading 'small in scale' is generally thought to be the one that fed the modern prefix.
items.cn: mikros 意为「小的、微小的」。一般认为「尺度上的小」这一读法是现代前缀的来源。

items.en: Oikonomikos described the management of a household, built from oikos 'house' and nemein 'to distribute, manage'.
items.cn: oikonomikos 指家宅的管理，由 oikos「家宅」与 nemein「分配、管理」构成。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek adjective as oeconomicus, still attached to the estate and the household rather than to a state.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊形容词作 oeconomicus，仍附着于产业与家宅，而非国家。

items.en: English economic, borrowed in the seventeenth century, widened from household management to the wealth and trade of a nation.
items.cn: 英语 economic 于十七世纪借入，从家宅管理扩展到国家的财富与贸易。

items.en: In the twentieth century the combining form for 'small' was attached to economic to mark the scale of a single unit.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，表示「小」的构词成分被接在 economic 之前，以标出单个单位的尺度。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the adjective is generally dated to the mid twentieth century, when analysis of single units was formally named, but no precise first citation is established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：一般认为这个形容词在二十世纪中期定名，与微观分析的制度化同步，但确切的首次书证尚未确立。

note.en: Group one lists words that share the same prefix but concern lenses, circuits or worlds; group two lists terms that stand close in meaning or form the opposite scale.
note.cn: 第一组是同用这个表示「小」的前缀、却分别关于透镜、电路与世界的词；第二组是语义相近或构成相反尺度的说法。

entries.definition: The same prefix plus Greek skopein 'to look': too small to be seen without a lens, a term of optics and biology rather than of money.
entries.definitionCN: 同一前缀加希腊语「看」：小到不借助透镜就看不见，属光学与生物学术语，与经济无关。

entries.definition: The prefix plus electronic: belonging to circuits and devices built on a very small scale.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀加「电子的」：属于以极小尺度制造的电路与器件。

entries.definition: The prefix plus Greek kosmos 'world': a small world that mirrors a larger one, with no economic sense.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀加希腊语「世界」：映照大世界的小世界，没有经济含义。

entries.definition: The same economic base with the prefix for 'large': it studies national totals, the exact mirror of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 同样的经济词干配表示「大」的前缀：研究全国总量，正是本词的反面。

entries.definition: From Latin pars 'part': in economics it describes analysis that examines one relation while holding the rest fixed.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 pars「部分」：在经济学中描述只考察一重关系、把其余条件保持不变的分析方式。

entries.definition: A transparent compound meaning 'at the scale of an individual company'; it states the unit without the technical label.
entries.definitionCN: 一个意思透明的复合词，指「以单个公司为尺度」；它朴素地说明单位，不带技术标签。

entries.definition: From dis- 'apart' plus grex 'flock': separated from a total into its individual units, the typical form of data used here.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语中表示「分开」的前缀加 grex「群」：从总量拆回各个单位，正是这类研究常用数据的形式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives rather than invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix for 'small' plus 'of the economy' gives a word for the economy seen one unit at a time.
normal.cn: 表示「小」的前缀加上「经济的」，得到的是把经济拆到单个单位来看的词。

normal.en: The family runs microeconomic, microeconomics, microeconomist, microeconometric.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 microeconomic、microeconomics、microeconomist、microeconometric。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: microeconomic theory, microeconomic analysis, microeconomic reform.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：微观经济理论、微观经济分析、微观经济改革。

normal.en: It forms a pair with macroeconomic: same base, opposite prefix, part versus whole.
normal.cn: 它与 macroeconomic 构成一对：同样的词干，相反的前缀，部分对整体。

normal.en: The phrase microeconomic data usually signals numbers gathered from individual units.
normal.cn: 「微观经济数据」这一搭配通常信号着从各个独立单位收集来的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a single ledger on a shop counter while the street's other shops stay out of frame.
abstract.cn: 想象柜台上摊着一本账，街上其余店铺都留在画面之外。

abstract.en: Picture a biologist adjusting a lens until one cell fills the whole field of view.
abstract.cn: 想象生物学家调着透镜，直到一个细胞占满整个视野。

abstract.en: Picture one stone lifted out of a mosaic so its own colour can be studied.
abstract.cn: 想象从镶嵌画里取出一块石子，好单独研究它自己的颜色。

examples.en: Microeconomic theory predicts how a single seller sets a price.
examples.cn: 微观经济理论预测单个卖方如何定价。

examples.en: The reform was microeconomic in scope, aimed at one industry rather than at national demand.
examples.cn: 这项改革的范围是微观经济的，针对一个行业而非全国需求。

examples.en: Calling a question microeconomic says nothing about how important the answer is.
examples.cn: 把一个问题称为微观经济的，并不说明它的答案有多重要。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「小」的前缀加「经济的」——把经济拆到一家店、一个柜台来看 → 微观经济的

root: 希腊 mikros「小的」+ oikonomikos（oikos「家宅」+ nemein「分配、管理」）→ 拉丁 oeconomicus → 英语 economic；二十世纪再加表示「小」的前缀，构成指单个主体层面的形容词。首见年份来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses hold one scale steady: a single unit. The line runs from the individual firm or household, to the single market it trades in, to the choices it makes, to the method that isolates one relation, to one industry as a target, to data gathered unit by unit, to the branch label, and finally to everyday choices made outside formal markets.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项守住同一个尺度：单个单位。这条线从单个企业或住户出发，走向它交易所在的单个市场、它所作的选择、隔离一重关系的方法、作为政策对象的单个行业、逐个单位收集的数据、分支名称，最后落到正式市场之外的日常选择。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a close-up of one ledger on a counter while the rest of the street stays outside the frame.
core.cn: 核心意象：柜台上一本账的特写，街上其余一切都被留在画面之外。

branches.en: UNIT AND ARENA: the agent is one firm or household, and the arena where it acts is one market.
branches.cn: 单位与场所：行动的主体是一家企业或一户人家，行动的场所是一个市场。

branches.en: CHOICE AND METHOD: what the unit chooses is studied by isolating a single relation.
branches.cn: 选择与方法：这个单位如何选择，靠隔离一重关系来研究。

branches.en: SECTOR AND DATA: one industry can be regulated, and unit-by-unit records make it measurable.
branches.cn: 行业与数据：单个行业可以被规制，逐个单位的记录又使它可测量。

branches.en: BRANCH LABEL: the scale became the name of one half of the discipline.
branches.cn: 分支名称：这一尺度成了一门学科其中一半的名字。

branches.en: EVERYDAY CHOICE: unit-level reasoning also covers households and time use outside formal markets.
branches.cn: 日常选择：单位层面的推理也覆盖正式市场之外的住户与时间分配。

intro.en: The word can be read morpheme by morpheme: a Greek prefix for size, a Greek noun for the household, a Greek verb for managing, and an English suffix that turns the stem into an adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词可以按语素逐个读出：表示尺度的希腊前缀、指家宅的希腊名词、表示管理的希腊动词，以及把词干变成形容词的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek oikonomikos reached English through Latin oeconomicus; the Latin noun oeconomia and the agent noun oeconomus belong to the same estate-management family.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 oikonomikos 经拉丁 oeconomicus 进入英语；拉丁名词 oeconomia 与施事名词 oeconomus 同属家产管理这一词族。

items.example: The prefix sets the scale of one unit.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出单个单位的尺度。

items.example: Mikros is generally thought to be the source of the prefix.
items.exampleCN: 一般认为这个希腊形容词就是该前缀的来源。

items.example: Oikos names the household that is managed.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指被管理的那一家人。

items.example: Nemein supplies the idea of managing a store.
items.exampleCN: 这个词提供了「管理储备」的意思。

items.example: The Greek adjective joined house to management.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊形容词把家宅与管理连在一起。

items.example: Latin kept the adjective close to the household.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语保留了它贴近家宅的含义。

items.example: English widened the adjective to the wealth of a state.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个形容词扩展到国家财富。

items.example: The suffix makes an adjective of a noun stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词词干变成形容词。

items.meaning: of single units in the economy
items.example: The adjective names the single-unit scale.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词指单个单位的尺度。

items.meaning: the study of single firms and markets
items.meaningCN: 研究单个企业与单个市场的学科
items.example: Microeconomics examines one market at a time.
items.exampleCN: 微观经济学一次考察一个市场。

latinEntries.structure: oeconomicus, oeconomica, oeconomicum (adj., first and second declension)

derivatives.zh: 微观的；单个主体层面的

definition_zh: 在……期间；在……过程中（强调事件展开的时间跨度，而非某一时点）
definition_en: during the progress or development of an event; over the span in which something unfolds
core_image: 一条河道从上游蜿蜒到下游，两岸景物随水流依次变化
scene: 修堤工程从春汛后开工，入冬前完工，其间挖土、砌石、验收依次进行。 Three design changes were made in the course of the dike project.
sceneCN: 这里取「在……过程中」（第 2 个义项：事件推进期间发生）；句意为堤坝工程进行期间做了三次设计变更。

pos.zh: 介词短语：在……期间；在……过程中

collocations.phrase: in the course of the trial
in the course of a year

senses.title: Across a period
senses.definition: used before a noun of time to say that something happens somewhere inside that span
senses.definitionCN: 用在表时间的名词前，表示某事在该时段之内发生
senses.example: Two repairs were carried out in the course of the decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这十年间进行了两次维修。
senses.why: Course is a running, and a run has length, so the phrase measures the span rather than a point.
senses.whyCN: 进程本是一次奔跑，而奔跑有长度，因此这个短语量的是时段，不是一个点。

senses.title: Inside a developing event
senses.titleCN: 过程义：在某事推进期间
senses.definition: used before the name of an event to say that something happens while that event unfolds
senses.definitionCN: 用在事件名称前，表示某事在该事件展开期间发生
senses.example: The plan was revised in the course of the survey.
senses.exampleCN: 调查进行期间，方案作了修订。
senses.why: An event has stages, and the phrase places the action somewhere along them.
senses.whyCN: 事件有阶段，这个短语把动作放在其中某处。

senses.title: As events unfold
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase with events it means as matters develop naturally, without a plan
senses.definitionCN: 在与事态一词的固定搭配中，表示随事情自然发展，并无预先安排
senses.example: It will become clear in the course of events.
senses.exampleCN: 随着事态发展，事情自会清楚。
senses.why: The plural of event suggests an open series, so the phrase sounds like the future revealing itself.
senses.whyCN: 事件的复数是开放序列，因此这个短语听起来像未来自行显现。

senses.title: Unlike a plain during
senses.titleCN: 辨义：与单个时间介词不同
senses.definition: it stresses the unfolding process, while a bare time preposition only marks the period
senses.definitionCN: 它强调展开的过程，而单个时间介词只标出时段
senses.example: In the course of the talks, the tone changed from hostile to calm.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈过程中，语气由敌对转为平和。
senses.why: The noun course adds movement, so the phrase suits change over time better than a neutral preposition.
senses.whyCN: 进程一词加了动感，所以这个短语比中性介词更适合描述随时间的变化。

senses.title: Legal and official proceedings
senses.titleCN: 程序义：在正式程序进行期间
senses.definition: in legal usage it covers steps taken while a case, hearing or inquiry is running
senses.definitionCN: 在法律用法中，指案件、听证或调查进行期间采取的步骤
senses.example: The document was filed in the course of the proceedings.
senses.exampleCN: 该文件是在诉讼进行期间提交的。
senses.why: Proceedings are a sequence of formal steps, which is why course fits the legal frame exactly.
senses.whyCN: 诉讼程序是一连串正式步骤，因此进程一词与这一法律框架严丝合缝。

senses.title: Across history
senses.definition: with history or a long era it means over the slow span in which large changes occur
senses.definitionCN: 与历史或漫长时期连用，指大变化在其中缓慢发生的长时段
senses.example: Trade routes shifted in the course of history.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易路线在历史进程中发生了转移。
senses.why: The phrase scales up: any span with internal development can be called a course.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语可以放大使用：任何内部有发展的时段都可称为一个进程。

senses.title: Within a short span
senses.definition: with a short unit of time it means the whole thing happened before that unit ended
senses.definitionCN: 与短时间单位连用，表示整件事在该单位结束前已经发生
senses.example: The whole procedure was completed in the course of a single morning.
senses.exampleCN: 整个程序在一个上午之内就完成了。
senses.why: Even a morning has parts, so the phrase still suggests a span with something happening inside it.
senses.whyCN: 即便一个上午也有若干部分，因此这个短语仍暗示时段内部发生了事情。

senses.title: Not a ship's route
senses.definition: although the noun can mean a direction taken, the phrase itself marks time rather than the path followed
senses.definitionCN: 尽管这个名词可指所取的方向，短语本身标的是时间，而非行经的路径
senses.example: In the course of the voyage marks the period, not the route the ship followed.
senses.exampleCN: 航行过程一语标出的是时段，不是船只走过的路线。
senses.why: With this preposition the noun loses its directional sense and keeps only duration.
senses.whyCN: 与这个介词连用时，名词失去方向义，只保留持续义。

intro.en: Course comes from Latin cursus, a running or a passage, from the verb currere, to run. The noun is secure; the English fixed phrase is modern.
intro.cn: 课程、进程一词来自拉丁语 cursus「奔跑、行程」，出自动词 currere「跑」。名词来源清楚；英语固定短语属近代。

items.en: Currere meant to run, and its participle and nouns spread across movement, flow and speed.
items.cn: currere 意为跑，其分词与名词形式扩展到运动、流动与速度。

items.en: Cursus named a run, a race or a passage across water, hence a route with length.
items.cn: cursus 指奔跑、赛程或渡水行程，因此是一条有长度的路线。

items.en: French kept the running and the path, and added the sense of a series of lessons.
items.cn: 法语保留了奔跑与路径，又发展出一系列课业的意思。

items.en: English holds direction, progression and a programme of study in one noun.
items.cn: 英语用同一个名词兼指方向、进展与课程体系。

items.en: The time-span frame settles in modern narrative and legal prose; first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 表时段的框架在近代叙事与法律文字中定型，首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the noun but means something else; the second group also marks time, with different force.
note.cn: 第一组共用这个名词却另有他义；第二组同样标时间，但力量不同。

entries.definition: It means at the proper time and takes no noun after it.
entries.definitionCN: 意为在适当时候，后面不带名词。

entries.definition: In speech it marks agreement or the obvious.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中表同意或显而易见。

entries.definition: Here the noun means a programme of lessons.
entries.definitionCN: 此处名词指课程体系。

entries.definition: The same frame with the noun events means as matters unfold.
entries.definitionCN: 同一框架配上事态一词，表示随事态展开。

entries.definition: A single preposition for a period, with no sense of development.
entries.definitionCN: 单个介词表时段，不含进展意味。

entries.definition: It stresses the entire span rather than events inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 强调整个时段，而非期间发生的事。

entries.definition: It links two actions happening at the same time.
entries.definitionCN: 连接同时发生的两件事。

entries.definition: It locates one moment inside an action.
entries.definitionCN: 把某一时刻定位在动作中间。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real running root, the real path and lesson senses, and the real time-span grammar.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实的奔跑词根、路径与课业的真实义项，以及真实的时段语法。

normal.en: A course is a run, and a run has length, so the phrase measures a span.
normal.cn: 进程是一次奔跑，奔跑有长度，所以这个短语量的是时段。

normal.en: The same noun also gives direction and a series of lessons.
normal.cn: 同一名词还给出方向与一系列课业。

normal.en: With events in the plural it means as matters unfold.
normal.cn: 与复数的世事连用，意为随事态展开。

normal.en: It suits change better than a bare time preposition.
normal.cn: 它比光秃秃的时间介词更适合描述变化。

normal.en: The ship's direction is not what the phrase marks.
normal.cn: 船行的方向并不是这个短语所标的东西。

abstract.en: Like a river seen from source to mouth: the water is always the same, the banks keep changing.
abstract.cn: 像从源头看到河口的整条河：水是同一股，两岸不断变化。

abstract.en: Like the middle pages of a book, where the story happens between opening and end.
abstract.cn: 像书的中间几页，故事在开头与结尾之间展开。

abstract.en: Like a season rather than a date: a stretch with weather inside it.
abstract.cn: 像一个季节而非一个日期：一段里面装着天气的日子。

examples.en: Several errors were found in the course of the inspection.
examples.cn: 检查过程中发现了若干错误。

examples.en: The site changed hands twice in the course of a year.
examples.cn: 该场地在一年之内两次易主。

examples.en: Attitudes to the practice shifted in the course of the century.
examples.cn: 对这种做法的态度在这一百年间发生了变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因 则 科斯 奥夫」——从上游到下游的一整条河：在……过程中

root: 核心名词意为进程，来自拉丁语 cursus「奔跑、行程」，出自动词 currere「跑」；该短语为近代定型，首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split by what fills the span: a period, a developing event, unfolding events, a contrast with plain during, legal proceedings, history, a short unit, and the exclusion of a ship's route.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按填入时段的内容区分：时段、展开中的事件、事态、与单个时间介词的对照、法律程序、历史、短时间单位，以及排除航向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river winding from source to mouth, the same water passing banks that keep changing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条河从源头蜿蜒到河口，同一股水流过不断变化的岸。

branches.en: THE SPAN: a decade, a morning or a century supplies the length that contains the event.
branches.cn: 时段：十年、一个上午或一个世纪提供容纳事件的长度。

branches.en: THE PROGRESS: an event or an open series of events carries the action along its stages.
branches.cn: 进程：一个事件或开放的事态序列把动作带到各个阶段。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST: the noun adds movement that a plain time preposition lacks.
branches.cn: 对照：名词带来的动感是单个时间介词所没有的。

branches.en: THE PROCEEDING: a case or a hearing is a formal run of steps.
branches.cn: 程序：案件或听证是一连串正式的步骤。

branches.en: THE SCALE AND THE LIMIT: history stretches the span wide, while a ship's route is excluded.
branches.cn: 尺度与边界：历史把时段拉得很宽，而船只路线被排除。

intro.en: The phrase rests on a Latin noun of running, so every use keeps a trace of movement through time.
intro.cn: 这个短语建在一个表奔跑的拉丁语名词上，因此每种用法都留着随时间推移的动感。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb is currere, to run, and its noun cursus, a running or a passage; English added the lesson sense later.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词是 currere「跑」，名词 cursus 意为奔跑、行程；英语后来加了课业义。

items.example: The verb supplies every member of this family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词提供了这一族所有成员。

items.example: The noun gives length and direction at once.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时给出长度与方向。

items.example: English holds three senses in one form.
items.exampleCN: 英语用一个形式兼指三种意思。

items.example: The participle sense survives in water and in time.
items.exampleCN: 分词义既留在水里，也留在时间上。

items.example: The idea of circulation keeps the running image.
items.exampleCN: 流通的观念保留了奔跑意象。

items.example: The Latin noun meant a running track, then a course.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁名词本指跑道，后指课程。

items.example: The phrase drops the complement and keeps the timing.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语省掉补语，只留时机。

items.example: The frame is standard in narrative and legal prose.
items.exampleCN: 这个框架在叙事与法律文字中是标准用法。

definition_zh: 厌恶；反感；憎恶的事物
definition_en: a strong feeling of dislike or repugnance toward something
core_image: 一闻到那气味，整个人就往后缩
scene: 她还没进门就捂住了鼻子。 She has an aversion to the smell of fresh paint.
sceneCN: 这里 aversion 指「厌恶、反感」（第 1 个义项：强烈的不喜欢）；句意：她一闻到新油漆的气味就本能地反感。

pos.zh: 厌恶；反感；憎恶的对象

derivatives.zh: 厌恶的；不愿的（aversion 的形容词基础）
令人反感的；引发回避的（aversion + -ive）

senses.title: A strong feeling of dislike
senses.definition: an intense and settled feeling of dislike toward a thing, act, or person
senses.definitionCN: 对某物、某行为或某人的强烈而稳固的厌恶感
senses.example: His aversion to crowds kept him out of stadiums.
senses.exampleCN: 他对人群的厌恶让他从不进体育场。
senses.why: The root means turned away: the feeling that pivots you from a thing.
senses.whyCN: 词根义为「转开」：那种把你从某物前转走的情绪。

senses.title: The object of dislike
senses.definition: the thing or person one feels aversion toward
senses.definitionCN: 引发或承受厌恶的具体对象
senses.example: Crowds became his chief aversion.
senses.exampleCN: 人群成了他最憎恶的东西。
senses.why: The feeling names what it points at, as loves and hates both do.
senses.whyCN: 情绪会转而指称其对象，爱与恨皆然。

senses.title: Reluctance or unwillingness
senses.definition: a disinclination to do something, milder than disgust
senses.definitionCN: 对做某事的不情愿，弱于憎恶
senses.example: She felt an aversion to signing the contract so soon.
senses.exampleCN: 她不愿这么快就签下合同。
senses.why: The turning away can be small: a hesitation rather than a recoil.
senses.whyCN: 「转开」可以很小：只是迟疑，而非后缩。

senses.title: Risk aversion in economics
senses.definition: the preference for certain outcomes over gambles of equal expected value
senses.definitionCN: 在期望值相同的情况下宁取确定结果的偏好
senses.example: Risk aversion explains why insurers stay in business.
senses.exampleCN: 风险厌恶解释了保险业长盛的原因。
senses.why: Decision theory borrowed the feeling-word for a measurable preference.
senses.whyCN: 决策理论借情绪词命名一种可测量的偏好。

senses.title: Conditioned avoidance in psychology
senses.definition: learned avoidance of a stimulus paired with discomfort
senses.definitionCN: 因刺激伴随不适而习得的回避反应
senses.example: Taste aversion stopped the wolves from baited traps.
senses.exampleCN: 味觉厌恶让狼群不再碰下了药的陷阱。
senses.why: One bad pairing is enough; the body remembers the turning away.
senses.whyCN: 一次糟糕的配对就足够；身体记住了那一次转开。

senses.title: Aversion therapy
senses.definition: treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with unpleasant stimuli
senses.definitionCN: 把不良行为与不快刺激配对的治疗方法
senses.example: Aversion therapy once paired smoking with mild shocks.
senses.exampleCN: 厌恶疗法曾把吸烟与轻微电击配对。
senses.why: Clinics trained the turning away on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 临床上有意训练这种「转开」反应。

senses.title: Moral repugnance
senses.definition: revulsion at cruelty, injustice, or corruption on principle
senses.definitionCN: 出于原则对残暴、不公或腐败的憎恶
senses.example: His aversion to cruelty drove him into law.
senses.exampleCN: 他对残暴的深恶痛绝驱使他投身法律。
senses.why: When the turning away is principled, it becomes a stance.
senses.whyCN: 当「转开」出于原则，它就成了一种立场。

senses.title: Instinctive physical recoil
senses.definition: an automatic bodily recoil at smells, textures, or sights
senses.definitionCN: 对气味、质感或画面不假思索的身体后退
senses.example: A visceral aversion made her drop the spoon.
senses.exampleCN: 本能的排斥让她丢下了勺子。
senses.why: This is the root at its most literal: the spine itself turns.
senses.whyCN: 这是词根最字面的呈现：连脊椎都在转开。

intro.en: Aversion comes from Latin aversio, a turning away, from avertere, from ab, away, plus vertere, to turn; English took both the noun and its adjective averse from the same participle.
intro.cn: aversion 出自拉丁语 aversio「转开」，源于 avertere，由 ab（离开）+ vertere（转）构成；英语的名词 aversion 与形容词 averse 同出一源。

items.en: The turn-root is the reconstructed wer-, to bend or turn.
items.cn: 「转」的词根出自重构词干 wer-「弯、转」。

items.en: averted combined ab, away, with vertere, to turn.
items.cn: 拉丁语 avertere 组合 ab「离开」与 vertere「转」。

items.en: aversio named the act or state of turning away, soon in moral contexts.
items.cn: aversio 指转开的动作或状态，很快用于道德语境。

items.en: Old and Middle French carried aversion with the psychological sense.
items.cn: 古法语与中古法语以 aversion 承载心理义项。

items.en: English adopted aversion around 1600, first of mental turning from objects of dislike.
items.cn: 英语约在 1600 年前后借入 aversion，先指心理上对所憎之物的背离。

items.en: Economics added risk aversion, and psychology added conditioned aversion.
items.cn: 经济学加入「风险厌恶」，心理学加入「条件性厌恶」。

note.en: Group one gathers the turning family and a spelling trap; group two gathers words of strong dislike.
note.cn: 第一组收「转」词族及拼写陷阱；第二组收强烈厌恶义场的词。

entries.definition: a rare, obsolete word for turning toward; one letter from aversion.
entries.definitionCN: 罕见的废词，义为「转向」；与 aversion 仅差一个字母。

entries.definition: the Late Latin source noun, a turning away.
entries.definitionCN: 晚期拉丁语源头名词，义为「转开」。

entries.definition: the verb of the family: to turn away or prevent.
entries.definitionCN: 词族中的动词：转开、防止。

entries.definition: strong, often moral, dislike; more formal than aversion.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈且常带道德色彩的憎恶；比 aversion 更正式。

entries.definition: sudden and violent disgust; aversion at its most physical.
entries.definitionCN: 突发而剧烈的恶心感；aversion 最生理性的一面。

entries.definition: mild dislike; the polite end of the scale.
entries.definitionCN: 轻微的不喜欢；厌恶刻度上温和的一端。

entries.definition: settled, intense hatred; beyond mere aversion.
entries.definitionCN: 根深蒂固的憎恨；超出单纯的厌恶。

entries.definition: unwillingness without emotional heat.
entries.definitionCN: 不带情绪温度的不情愿。

normalIntro.en: Keep the family visible: avert, averse, aversion are one turning in three grammars.
normalIntro.cn: 看清词族：avert、averse、aversion 是同一个「转」的三种语法形态。

normal.en: av- from ab- means away; -sion makes the turning a noun.
normal.cn: av- 出自 ab-「离开」；-sion 把「转」变成名词。

normal.en: have an aversion to is the standard pattern; note the preposition to.
normal.cn: 固定句型 have an aversion to，注意介词用 to。

normal.en: risk aversion is the economics term every exam loves.
normal.cn: risk aversion 是考试偏爱的经济学术语：风险厌恶。

normal.en: aversion therapy is the clinical collocation.
normal.cn: aversion therapy 是临床搭配：厌恶疗法。

normal.en: Plural aversions lists your several dislikes.
normal.cn: 复数 aversions 可列举多种厌恶。

abstract.en: Feel the whole body step back one measured pace.
abstract.cn: 感觉整个人向后退了整整齐齐的一步。

abstract.en: Aversion is a door your mind shuts before thinking.
abstract.cn: aversion 是理智开口之前心先关上的门。

abstract.en: Picture the compass needle refusing a direction it once held.
abstract.cn: 想象罗盘针拒绝它曾指向的方向。

examples.en: He confessed an aversion to loud music of any era.
examples.cn: 他坦承对任何年代的吵闹音乐都很反感。

examples.en: Her aversions ran from cilantro to committee meetings.
examples.cn: 她的厌恶清单从香菜一路排到委员会会议。

examples.en: Investors' risk aversion rose sharply after the crash.
examples.cn: 崩盘后投资者的风险厌恶急剧上升。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「恶我神」——那味道一飘来就「恶我神」，魂儿都厌恶得缩回去了

root: 出自晚期拉丁语 aversio「转开」，为 avertere（ab- 离开 + vertere 转）的名词化形式，与 avert、averse 同族；约 1600 年经法语进入英语，先表心理背离，近现代被经济学与心理学借作术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the turning away: the feeling, its object, plain reluctance, and the technical senses that economics and psychology built on it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项顺着「转开」展开：情绪本身、情绪对象、单纯的不情愿，以及经济学与心理学在此之上建立的技术义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the whole body stepping back before the mind explains why.
core.cn: 核心意象：理智还没解释，身体已先退后一步。

branches.en: THE FEELING SIDE: the dislike and the thing it points at.
branches.cn: 情感一面：厌恶本身与它指向的对象。

branches.en: THE WILLINGNESS SIDE: mild, everyday reluctance.
branches.cn: 意愿一面：日常而轻微的不情愿。

branches.en: THE ECONOMIC SIDE: measured risk aversion.
branches.cn: 经济一面：可度量的风险厌恶。

branches.en: THE CLINICAL SIDE: conditioned and therapeutic avoidance.
branches.cn: 临床一面：条件性回避与厌恶疗法。

branches.en: THE DEEP SIDE: moral principle and bodily recoil.
branches.cn: 深层一面：道德原则与生理排斥。

intro.en: Aversion is the participle aversus plus the noun ending -io: a turning, made into a thing.
intro.cn: aversion 由分词 aversus 加名词词尾 -io 构成：把「转开」变成一个事物。

latinIntro.en: Latin made -tio nouns from participles, and French -tion passed them into English by the hundred.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 -tio 由分词造名词，法语 -tion 又把成百上千个这样的词送进英语。

definition_zh: 宪法权利；宪法保障的基本权利；宪法上的权利
definition_en: a right guaranteed to people by a country's constitution and placed beyond ordinary legislative change
core_image: 一本摊开的宪法摆在法院台阶上，书页中一条被红线框住的条款，正挡住一扇正在关上的门
scene: 法院在判决中确认，集会自由属于宪法权利，政府不得以行政命令取消。 The court held that freedom of assembly is a constitutional right which no administrative order may cancel.
sceneCN: 这里指「宪法明文保障、可用来对抗政府的基本权利」，对应第 1 个义项：由宪法确认、政府不能随意取消的权利；句意为法院认定集会自由属于此类权利。画面要点：摊开的宪法、被红线框住的条款、被挡住的门。

pos.zh: 宪法权利（可数，常用复数形式，指一组由宪法保障的权利）

derivatives.zh: 宪法的；符合宪法的（由「宪法」这一名词加形容词后缀构成，指与根本组织相关或经其许可）
依宪法地；从宪法角度看（形容词加副词后缀，指以宪法为尺度）
违宪的（否定前缀加形容词，指与宪法条文相抵触）
宪法；根本组织（由拉丁语「设立、安排」的动词加名词词尾构成，指一国根本结构的成文安排）

senses.title: A right written into the charter
senses.definition: an entitlement that the constitution itself names or clearly implies, so that it does not depend on an ordinary statute
senses.definitionCN: 宪法本身列明或明显蕴含的应享之权，因此不依赖普通法律而存在
senses.example: The court held that freedom of assembly is a constitutional right which no administrative order may cancel.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定集会自由属于宪法权利，任何行政命令都不能取消。
senses.why: The phrase joins a word for the state's founding arrangement to a word for a just claim, so the right is anchored in the document that creates the state.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把表示国家根本安排的名词与表示正当主张的名词连在一起，权利因此被锚定在创制国家的那份文件上。

senses.title: A shield against government action
senses.definition: a right that can be asserted against the state, limiting what officials may do to a person
senses.definitionCN: 可以针对国家主张的权利，用以限制官员能对个人做什么
senses.example: A constitutional right limits the search of a private home without a warrant.
senses.exampleCN: 宪法权利限制没有搜查令时对私人住宅的搜查。
senses.why: Most such rights are phrased as prohibitions on government, so the right works less as a grant than as a fence around power.
senses.whyCN: 这类权利多以对政府的禁令形式表述，因此它更像围住权力的一道栅栏，而不是一项授予。

senses.title: A rank above ordinary law
senses.titleCN: 位阶高于普通法律的权利
senses.definition: a right that ordinary legislation cannot remove or dilute, because it stands at a higher level in the legal order
senses.definitionCN: 普通立法不能取消或稀释的权利，因为它在法律秩序中处于更高位阶
senses.example: Because it is a constitutional right, the guarantee survives changes in the statute book.
senses.exampleCN: 由于它是宪法权利，这项保障不会因普通法令的变动而消失。
senses.why: The word for a founding arrangement implies a hierarchy: what is set at the base cannot be moved by what is built on top of it.
senses.whyCN: 表示根本安排的那个词本身就含有一个层级：设在基底的东西，不能被建在其上的东西挪动。

senses.title: A right that resists restriction
senses.titleCN: 难以被限制、需经严格审查的权利
senses.definition: a right that a court will let the state restrict only for a compelling reason and by the narrowest means
senses.definitionCN: 只有在理由极为充分、且手段最小时，法院才允许国家加以限制的权利
senses.example: Restrictions on a constitutional right must pass strict scrutiny.
senses.exampleCN: 对宪法权利的限制必须通过严格审查。
senses.why: Rank alone does not protect a right; the higher rank is enforced through a stricter test that the government must satisfy.
senses.whyCN: 位阶本身并不保护权利；较高的位阶是通过一套更严格的检验来落实的，而举证责任在政府一方。

senses.title: Procedural guarantees
senses.definition: rights concerned with how decisions are made, such as notice, a hearing and a reasoned decision
senses.definitionCN: 关乎决定如何作出的权利，例如获得通知、获得听审与获得说明理由的决定
senses.example: Due process is the constitutional right that the hearing must actually take place.
senses.exampleCN: 正当程序这项宪法权利意味着听审必须真正举行。
senses.why: A person cannot enjoy substantive rights without a procedure to claim them, so the charter protects the road as well as the destination.
senses.whyCN: 没有主张的程序，人就无法享有实体权利，因此宪法既保护目的地，也保护道路。

senses.title: Substantive freedoms
senses.definition: rights protecting what a person may say, believe, own or do, rather than how a decision is reached
senses.definitionCN: 保护个人可以说什么、信什么、拥有什么、做什么的权利，而不是关于决定如何作出的权利
senses.example: Speech and worship are substantive constitutional rights in many countries.
senses.exampleCN: 在许多国家，言论与礼拜都是实体性的宪法权利。
senses.why: The same document that sets out procedure also marks out areas the state may not enter at all, and those areas are the substantive core.
senses.whyCN: 同一份文件既规定了程序，也划出了国家完全不得进入的区域，那些区域就是实体核心。

senses.title: A right a court can enforce
senses.titleCN: 法院可以强制执行的权利
senses.definition: a right that a person may bring before a court and obtain a remedy for its breach
senses.definitionCN: 个人可以提交法院、并在其被侵害时获得救济的权利
senses.example: Without a remedy, a constitutional right would be only a promise on paper.
senses.exampleCN: 没有救济，宪法权利就只是纸上的承诺。
senses.why: A claim that cannot be heard is not a right in practice, so the enforceable sense grows from the legal meaning of a right as something a court will act on.
senses.whyCN: 不能被审理的主张在实践中不是权利，因此「可强制执行」这一层从权利的法律含义中长出来：法院会为之采取行动。

senses.title: A guarantee that resists amendment
senses.titleCN: 难以通过修宪变动的保障
senses.definition: a right whose removal would require the special and difficult procedure of constitutional amendment
senses.definitionCN: 要取消它必须走修宪这一特殊而艰难的程序的权利
senses.example: Changing that constitutional right would require a two-thirds vote in both houses.
senses.exampleCN: 要改变那项宪法权利，需在两院各取得三分之二多数。
senses.why: When a guarantee is placed in the charter, the cost of removing it rises from a simple majority to an amendment, and that cost is itself part of the protection.
senses.whyCN: 当一项保障被放进宪法，取消它的成本就从简单多数上升到修宪，而这个成本本身就是保护的一部分。

intro.en: Constitutional joins the noun constitution to an adjective ending; constitution descends from Latin constituere 'to set up'. Right is a Germanic word, not a Latin borrowing, though it shares an ancient root with Latin rectus. The phrase itself is a modern legal compound.
intro.cn: constitutional 由名词 constitution 加形容词词尾构成；constitution 出自拉丁语 constituere「设立」。right 是日耳曼语词，并非拉丁语借词，但它与拉丁语 rectus 共享一个古老词根。整个短语属现代法律复合词。

items.en: Statuere 'to set up, establish' is the verb at the base of the family, carrying the image of placing something so that it stands.
items.cn: statuere 意为「竖立、设立」，是整个词族的基干动词，含有把某物安置得能立住的形象。

items.en: Constituere joined the prefix for 'together' with statuere and described arranging a body, an office or an institution.
items.cn: constituere 把表示「共同」的前缀与 statuere 结合，描述对一个团体、职位或机构的安排。

items.en: Constitutio named an arrangement or an ordinance, and in Roman law it could mean an enactment issued by the emperor.
items.cn: constitutio 指一种安排或法令，在罗马法中可指皇帝颁布的敕令。

items.en: In English the noun came to mean the fundamental arrangement of a state, and its adjective followed in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 在英语中，这个名词逐渐指一个国家的根本安排，其形容词形式在十七世纪出现。

items.en: Riht meant 'straight, just, right' and supplied the word for a just claim long before anyone attached it to a written charter.
items.cn: riht 意为「直的、正当的、对的」，在人们把它与成文宪章联系起来之前很久，就已用来指正当的主张。

items.en: The phrase took its present sense in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, as written charters and judicial review spread. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 随着成文宪法与司法审查的普及，这个短语在十八与十九世纪取得现今含义。年代为约数。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same Latin verb for setting up; the second group holds other kinds of right that are often confused with this one.
note.cn: 第一组是由同一个表示「设立」的拉丁动词构成的词；第二组是常与本词混淆的其他类型的权利。

entries.definition: The fundamental text or arrangement of a state; it is the source that the adjective describes, not the right itself.
entries.definitionCN: 一个国家的根本文本或根本安排；它是形容词所描述的来源，而不是权利本身。

entries.definition: Forming an essential part of something; it describes what makes a thing what it is, not what a charter guarantees.
entries.definitionCN: 构成某物本质部分的；它描述使一物成为该物的要素，而不是宪章保障的内容。

entries.definition: A part of a whole, or a voter in a district; the same verb underlies it, but neither sense concerns a guaranteed entitlement.
entries.definitionCN: 整体的组成部分，或选区中的选民；同一个动词是其底子，但两种意思都不涉及受保障的权利。

entries.definition: A right treated as basic to a legal order; in many systems it is the same set of guarantees, but the label stresses importance rather than the source document.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为某一法律秩序之基础的权利；在许多法系中它指同一组保障，但这个说法强调重要性而非来源文件。

entries.definition: A right given by an ordinary law, which the legislature can also narrow or repeal; it stands lower than the constitutional kind.
entries.definitionCN: 由普通法律赋予的权利，立法机关也可加以缩小或废止；它的位阶低于宪法权利。

entries.definition: Any entitlement recognised by law, whatever its source; it covers constitutional, statutory and judge-made rights alike.
entries.definitionCN: 法律承认的任何应享之权，不问来源；它同时涵盖宪法、法律与判例产生的权利。

entries.definition: A right said to belong to people by nature, before any document; it is a moral argument that a charter may later record.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为人生而固有、先于任何文件的权利；它是一种道德主张，宪章后来可能把它记录下来。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin verb for setting up, the Germanic word for a just claim, real derived words and real legal phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示「设立」的动词、日耳曼语中表示正当主张的词、真实派生词与真实法律用语。

normal.en: A constitution sets things up; a constitutional right is one of the things it sets beyond ordinary law.
normal.cn: 宪法把事物设立起来；宪法权利就是它设立在普通法律之上的那些事物之一。

normal.en: The family runs constitution, constitutional, constitutionally and unconstitutional.
normal.cn: 同族词包括「宪法」、形容词、副词与否定形式。

normal.en: Rights in a charter act as fences around government power rather than gifts handed out.
normal.cn: 宪章中的权利更像围住政府权力的栅栏，而不是被分发的礼物。

normal.en: A statutory right can be repealed by a new statute; a constitutional one needs an amendment.
normal.cn: 法律权利可被新法律废止；宪法权利则需要修宪。

normal.en: The Germanic word for right is related to the Latin word for straight, which is why a right and a straight line feel connected.
normal.cn: 表示「权利」的日耳曼语词与拉丁语中表示「直」的词同源，所以权利与直线在感觉上相通。

abstract.en: Picture a stone slab laid at the bottom of a building, so deep that later floors cannot move it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石板铺在建筑的最底层，埋得那样深，以至于上面各层都无法挪动它。

abstract.en: Picture a fence drawn on a map before any building is allowed inside it.
abstract.cn: 想象在任何人获准进入之前，地图上先画好的一道栅栏。

abstract.en: Picture a door that can be closed by many hands but opened only by a key kept in a locked drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，许多人都能关上，却只有一把存放在上锁抽屉里的钥匙才能打开。

examples.en: The right to a hearing is a constitutional right in that system.
examples.cn: 在该法系中，获得听审的权利是一项宪法权利。

examples.en: Officials argued that the order did not touch any constitutional right.
examples.cn: 官员辩称该命令并未触及任何宪法权利。

examples.en: A constitutional right cannot be abolished by a simple majority vote.
examples.cn: 宪法权利不能被简单多数票废除。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「宪法里的那张票」——把权利写在国家根本章程上，就成了谁都拿不走的一张票。

root: constitution 出自拉丁语 constituere「设立、安排」，由表示「共同」的前缀与 statuere「竖立」构成，再经 constitutio「安排、敕令」进入英语；right 出自古英语 riht「直的、正当的」，属日耳曼语词，与拉丁语 rectus「直的」同源，源头可追至印欧语中表示「使直、统治」的词根，该词根形式属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings circle one anchor: a claim fixed in the founding document. From that anchor come the shield against the state, the rank above ordinary law, the strict test that guards the rank, the split between procedure and substance, the remedy that makes the claim real, and the high cost of amendment that keeps it in place.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个锚点：固定在建国文件中的一项主张。从这个锚点分出：对抗国家的盾牌、高于普通法律的位阶、守护位阶的严格检验、程序与实体的分工、使主张成真的救济，以及使它留在原处的修宪高成本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clause printed in the founding charter, standing between a person and the machinery of the state.
core.cn: 核心意象：印在建国宪章里的一条条款，立在个人与国家机器之间。

branches.en: THE ANCHOR: the entitlement named in the charter itself.
branches.cn: 锚点：宪章本身列明的应享之权。

branches.en: SHIELD AND REMEDY: the claim against the state, and the court that can act on it.
branches.cn: 盾牌与救济：针对国家的主张，以及能据此行动的法院。

branches.en: RANK AND RIGIDITY: a level above ordinary law, and the amendment cost that keeps it there.
branches.cn: 位阶与刚性：高于普通法律的层级，以及把它留在那里的修宪成本。

branches.en: LIMIT AND PROCEDURE: the strict test for restriction, and the guarantees about how decisions are made.
branches.cn: 限制与程序：限制权利时的严格检验，以及关于决定如何作出的保障。

branches.en: SUBSTANCE: the freedoms the state may not enter at all.
branches.cn: 实体：国家完全不得进入的那些自由领域。

intro.en: Two histories meet in this phrase: a Latin verb for establishing, which gives the whole constitution family, and a Germanic adjective for straightness and justice, which gives right and its derived words.
intro.cn: 两段历史在这个短语里相遇：一个表示「设立」的拉丁动词给出整个「宪法」词族，一个表示「直」与「正当」的日耳曼形容词给出「权利」及其派生词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below belong to the constitution side of the phrase. Right has a Latin cousin meaning 'straight', but the English word itself was not borrowed from that cousin.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式属于短语中「宪法」这一边。「权利」有一个意为「直」的拉丁同源词，但英语中的这个词本身并非从该同源词借入。

items.meaning: a basic entitlement fixed in the founding charter
items.meaningCN: 固定在建国宪章中的基本应享之权
items.example: The court treated the claim as a constitutional right.
items.exampleCN: 法院把这项主张视为宪法权利。

items.meaning: of or consistent with the constitution
items.example: The reform required a constitutional amendment.
items.exampleCN: 这项改革需要一次宪法修正。

items.meaning: the fundamental arrangement of a state
items.example: The constitution divides power among three branches.
items.exampleCN: 宪法把权力分给三个分支。

items.meaning: the quality of being consistent with the charter
items.example: The court reviewed the constitutionality of the statute.
items.exampleCN: 法院审查了该法令是否符合宪法。

items.example: The search was ruled unconstitutional.
items.exampleCN: 那次搜查被裁定违宪。

items.meaning: a just claim; straight and correct
items.meaningCN: 正当的主张；直的、正确的
items.example: Every citizen has the right to petition.
items.exampleCN: 每个公民都有请愿的权利。

items.meaning: in accordance with a just claim
items.example: The heir returned to his rightful place.
items.exampleCN: 继承人回到了他合法应有的位置。

items.example: She rightfully demanded a receipt.
items.exampleCN: 她正当地要求一张收据。

items.meaning: a legal priority to pass over land or road
items.example: Pedestrians have the right of way at this crossing.
items.exampleCN: 在这个路口行人有优先通行权。

latinEntries.meaning: to set up, cause to stand

derivatives.zh: 宪法的；符合宪法的（由「宪法」这一名词加形容词后缀构成，指与根本组织相关或经其许可）
依宪法地（形容词加副词后缀，指以宪法为尺度）
违宪的（否定前缀加形容词，指与宪法条文相抵触）
合法的；正当的（表示「正当」的名词加形容词后缀，指依正当主张而应得）

definition_zh: 劳动力；全体员工；在岗人员总数
definition_en: all the people who work in an organization, industry or country, considered as a body
core_image: 厂门口的招工启事与车间里三班倒的人，人事部在册页上清点人数
scene: 厂区门口贴着招工启事，车间三班倒，人事部正在清点在册人数。 The plant's workforce has grown by a third since the new line opened.
sceneCN: 这里 workforce 指「某单位的全部在岗人员」（第 1 个义项：一个组织或地区里工作的全体人员）；句意为新生产线投产以来，这家工厂的员工总数增加了三分之一。图中可辨识物件：招工启事、打卡机、排班表、在册名单、安全帽。

pos.zh: 劳动力；全体员工；劳动力总量（可数或不可数）

senses.title: All the people who work in one organization
senses.titleCN: 一个组织里的全体工作人员
senses.definition: the whole body of people employed by a single firm, plant or institution
senses.definitionCN: 一家公司、工厂或机构雇用的全部人员
senses.example: The plant's workforce has grown by a third since the new line opened.
senses.exampleCN: 新生产线投产以来，这家工厂的员工总数增加了三分之一。
senses.why: Work and force join to mean 'the strength available for work', and an organization's strength is simply the people on its books.
senses.whyCN: work 与 force 组合指「可供工作的力量」，而一个组织的力量就是它名册上的人。

senses.title: The total labour supply of a place
senses.titleCN: 一个地区的劳动力总量
senses.definition: the number of people in a country or region who are available for work
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家或地区里可供使用的工作人数
senses.example: Half the national workforce is now employed in services.
senses.exampleCN: 全国劳动力目前有一半受雇于服务业。
senses.why: Economics needs a single figure for the labour a place can put to use, and the compound supplies exactly that countable body.
senses.whyCN: 经济学需要一个数字表示一个地方能投入的劳动，这个复合词恰好提供了这样一个可清点的整体。

senses.title: The staff a manager can deploy
senses.titleCN: 管理者可调配的员工队伍
senses.definition: the body of employees treated as a resource to be assigned and moved
senses.definitionCN: 被当作可分配、可调动的资源来看待的全体员工
senses.example: The new director reorganized the workforce into three regional teams.
senses.exampleCN: 新主管把员工队伍重组为三个区域团队。
senses.why: The second element of the compound is the same word for physical force, so people are spoken of as a strength to be directed.
senses.whyCN: 复合词的第二部分与「力量」同词，因此人被说成一股可被调遣的力量。

senses.title: The people assigned to one task
senses.definition: the particular group of workers given over to a project or operation
senses.definitionCN: 专门投入某个项目或作业的那一群工作者
senses.example: A workforce of two hundred was assembled for the tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 为这条隧道集中了两百人的施工队伍。
senses.why: Because the compound names a body rather than an individual, it can be counted for a single undertaking.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词指一个整体而非个人，因此可以按单项工程来计人数。

senses.title: The employed part of the population
senses.definition: those who currently hold paid work, as contrasted with the unemployed
senses.definitionCN: 当前有报酬工作的人，与失业者相对
senses.example: The survey separated the workforce from those who had stopped looking.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查把在业人口与已停止求职的人分开统计。
senses.why: Statistical use needs a line between people with jobs and people without, and this compound marks the side with jobs.
senses.whyCN: 统计上需要在有工作与没工作的人之间划一条线，这个复合词标记的是有工作的一侧。

senses.title: The collective skills of the staff
senses.titleCN: 员工技术与能力的总和
senses.definition: the sum of what the employees can do, treated as an asset of the firm
senses.definitionCN: 员工能力的总和，被视为公司的一项资产
senses.example: The merger was valued mainly for its experienced workforce.
senses.exampleCN: 这次合并的价值主要在于对方有经验的员工队伍。
senses.why: Once 'force' is read as capacity, the compound can mean capacity in the sense of skill rather than head count.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 force 读作「能力」，这个复合词便可指技能意义上的能力，而不只是人头数。

senses.title: Organized labour in an industry
senses.titleCN: 行业层面的劳动者群体
senses.definition: the workers of a trade or sector viewed as one interest
senses.definitionCN: 把某个行业或部门的工人视为一个整体利益
senses.example: The union speaks for a workforce of nine thousand.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工会代表九千名工人。
senses.why: Collective bargaining requires a single counterpart, so the compound also names workers as an organized body.
senses.whyCN: 集体谈判需要一个单一对手方，因此这个复合词也把工人称作一个有组织的整体。

senses.title: The pool of people who could be drawn into work
senses.titleCN: 可被吸纳进工作的潜在人力
senses.definition: the wider reserve, including those not yet working, from which employers may recruit
senses.definitionCN: 包括尚未工作的人在内的更大储备，雇主可从中招人
senses.example: Childcare costs keep many trained people out of the workforce.
senses.exampleCN: 托育费用使许多受过训练的人无法进入劳动力队伍。
senses.why: When the word is used of what is 'in' or 'out of' it, the reference shifts from those working to all who might work.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词被说成「在」或「不在」其中时，所指便从正在工作的人转向所有可能工作的人。

intro.en: Workforce is a modern English compound, joining the native noun work with force, which came into English from Old French and ultimately from Latin fortis 'strong'. It belongs to the language of management and national accounts. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: workforce 是近代英语复合词，由英语本族名词 work 加 force 构成；force 经古法语进入英语，最终出自拉丁 fortis「强壮」。它属于管理与国民核算的语言。年代均为约数。

items.en: Weorc meant 'work, deed, something made', from a Germanic root shared by German Werk and Dutch werk; it is native, not borrowed.
items.cn: weorc 意为「工作、行为、做成之物」，出自与德语 Werk、荷兰语 werk 同源的日耳曼词根，是英语本族成分，不是借词。

items.en: Fortis meant 'strong'; its noun fortia gave Old French force 'strength, power, violence', which English borrowed.
items.cn: fortis 意为「强壮」；其名词 fortia 演成古法语 force「力量、权力、强力」，英语借入后者。

items.en: The two words were joined in the twentieth century to name the labour available to an employer or a country, a term that belongs to personnel management and national accounting.
items.cn: 两个词在 20 世纪合起来指雇主或国家可用的劳动，这一术语属于人事管理与国民核算。

items.en: Earlier 'force of work' could mean the strength a task demands; the modern sense keeps only the people, and the strength they represent moves into the background.
items.cn: 早期「工作的力量」可指任务所需的气力；现代义只保留人，人所代表的力量退到背景里。

items.en: Labour statistics adopted the compound for the count of people in work, and from there it entered ordinary news language.
items.cn: 劳动统计采用这个复合词来计在业人数，此后它进入日常新闻语言。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the first printed use of the closed compound is not firmly dated, and whether it arose in American personnel writing or in British labour statistics is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个连写复合词最早印行于何时没有可靠年代，它起于美国人事实务写作还是英国劳动统计，亦无定论。

note.en: The first group holds compounds and near forms built on the same two words; the second holds terms for the same people counted a different way.
note.cn: 第一组是用同样两个词构成的复合词与形近形式；第二组是用另一种口径统计同一群人的术语。

entries.definition: The spaced spelling of the same term; modern style guides prefer the closed form for the collective sense.
entries.definitionCN: 同一术语的分写形式；现代体例指南在集合义上更倾向连写。

entries.definition: The building or setting where work happens; it shares the first element but names a location.
entries.definitionCN: 工作发生的场所；共享第一个成分，但指地点。

entries.definition: The amount of work assigned to a person or team; it measures the task, not the staff.
entries.definitionCN: 分配给个人或团队的工作量；衡量任务，不衡量人员。

entries.definition: A desk or machine set up for one worker; it names equipment rather than the body of staff.
entries.definitionCN: 为一名工作者配置的工位或机器；指设备而非员工整体。

entries.definition: The employees of a particular organization taken as a group; it rarely extends to a whole country.
entries.definitionCN: 某一组织的员工整体；很少扩展到整个国家。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same statistical idea, often including the unemployed who are seeking work.
entries.definitionCN: 同一统计概念的英式拼法，常包含正在求职的失业者。

entries.definition: The people employed by an organization, viewed through hiring and records; it sounds official.
entries.definitionCN: 从招聘与档案角度看的一个组织的受雇者；语气正式。

entries.definition: An older term for the number of people available for work, framed as physical capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 较早的术语，指可用人数，框定为体能式的能力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real relatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合结构、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Work plus force: the strength a place can put to work is the people on its books.
normal.cn: work 加 force：一个地方能投入工作的力量，就是它名册上的人。

normal.en: The family runs work, worker, workplace, workload, workforce.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 work、worker、workplace、workload、workforce。

normal.en: Fixed phrases place the word: skilled workforce, aging workforce, enter the workforce.
normal.cn: 固定说法给出位置：技术型劳动力、老龄化劳动力、进入职场。

normal.en: Force here is the Latin fortis 'strong', so the second half is about strength, not coercion.
normal.cn: 这里的 force 是拉丁 fortis「强壮」，因此后半讲的是力量，不是强制。

normal.en: The word is a body, so it takes a singular verb: the workforce has grown.
normal.cn: 这个词指一个整体，因此动词用单数：员工总数已经增长。

abstract.en: Picture a reservoir behind a dam, measured in people rather than litres.
abstract.cn: 想象坝后的一座水库，只是它的计量单位是人而不是升。

abstract.en: Picture a shift board where every name is a slot that can be filled.
abstract.cn: 想象一块排班板，每个名字都是可以被填上的格子。

abstract.en: Picture a firm's balance sheet listing skills where money usually goes.
abstract.cn: 想象一张公司资产负债表，在通常写钱的那一栏写着技能。

examples.en: The factory retrained its workforce rather than closing the plant.
examples.cn: 这家工厂选择再培训员工，而不是关厂。

examples.en: An aging workforce changes what products a town can sell.
examples.cn: 劳动力老龄化会改变一座城镇能卖什么产品。

examples.en: Automation cut the workforce by half in five years.
examples.cn: 自动化在五年内把员工人数削减了一半。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「work（工作）+ force（力量）」——一个单位能投入工作的那股力量 → 全体员工、劳动力

root: 英语本族 work（古英语 weorc「工作」）+ force（古法语 force，出自拉丁 fortis「强壮」）。20 世纪合成，指雇主或国家可用的劳动；force 在此取「力量」义而非「强制」义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the people on one firm's books and widen step by step: a country's supply, a manager's resource, a project's crew, the employed half of a population, its skills, an organized body and finally the reserve outside the door.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一家公司名册上的人开始，逐级放宽：一个国家的供给、管理者手中的资源、某项目的队伍、人口中的在业部分、这些人的技能、一个有组织的群体，最后是门外那支储备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate with a hiring notice on it, and a roster inside counting the people who pass through.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道门，门上贴着招工信，门内一本名册在清点进出的人。

branches.en: FROM ONE FIRM TO ONE COUNTRY: the same body is counted at the scale of an employer and at the scale of a nation.
branches.cn: 由一家到一国：同一个整体既可按雇主规模计，也可按国家规模计。

branches.en: RESOURCE AND CREW: once people are a strength, they can be assigned to a department or to a single job.
branches.cn: 资源与队伍：人一旦成为一股力量，便可被分派到某个部门或某项工程。

branches.en: COUNT AND CAPACITY: statistics count heads, while valuation counts what those heads can do.
branches.cn: 人数与能力：统计数人头，估值则数这些人会做什么。

branches.en: ORGANIZED BODY: bargaining turns the crowd into a single counterpart.
branches.cn: 有组织的整体：谈判把人群变成一个单一对手方。

branches.en: THE RESERVE OUTSIDE: the word also reaches people not yet working, who could still be drawn in.
branches.cn: 门外的储备：这个词也伸向尚未工作、但仍可被吸纳的人。

intro.en: The compound joins a native English noun to a Latin-derived noun, so its two halves belong to different layers of the vocabulary and bring different relatives.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把英语本族名词与拉丁来源名词接在一起，两半分属词汇的不同层次，也带来不同的同族词。

latinIntro.en: Old English weorc gives work, worker, workshop and workload; Latin fortis gives force, forte, effort and reinforce.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 weorc 衍生 work、worker、workshop 与 workload；拉丁 fortis 衍生 force、forte、effort 与 reinforce。

items.structure: work (native English noun, from Old English weorc)
items.meaningCN: 为达成某事而做的活动
items.example: The first half names the activity itself.
items.exampleCN: 前半部分命名活动本身。

items.structure: force (English noun, from Old French, from Latin fortia)
items.example: The second half names strength rather than compulsion.
items.exampleCN: 后半部分指力量，而非强迫。

items.example: Each worker signs the roster at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 每名工人在门口的名册上签到。

items.example: The workplace has two shifts.
items.exampleCN: 这个工作场所有两个班次。

items.example: The workload doubled after the merger.
items.exampleCN: 合并后工作量翻倍。

items.example: The plan is workable within a year.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划一年内可行。

items.example: Her forceful argument carried the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 她有力的论证使会议倒向她一边。

items.example: Extra staff reinforced the night crew.
items.exampleCN: 额外人手增援了夜班。

definition_zh: 现实主义；写实主义；务实态度；实在论
definition_en: the attempt to show things as they really are, or the belief that reality exists independently of the mind
core_image: 画家把街角面包店的旧招牌、脏围裙与找零的手一分不差地画下来
scene: 画家在街角支起画架，把面包店的旧招牌与顾客的皱纹一起画进画里。 The painter set up his easel at the corner and recorded the bakery's worn sign and its customers' wrinkles with realism.
sceneCN: 这里指「如实描绘日常生活的写实手法」（第 1 个义项：艺术中的现实主义）；句意为画家在街角支起画架，用写实手法记录旧招牌与顾客的皱纹。可辨识物件：画架、面包店招牌、顾客、皱纹。

pos.zh: 现实主义；写实主义（艺术与文学）
务实态度；实在论（哲学用语）

forms.label: 复数形式（指多种现实主义）

derivatives.zh: 现实主义者；写实的（由基础词加表示「信奉者」的后缀构成，语义收窄为立场身份）
现实的；写实的（由表示现实主义者的词加表示「与……有关的」后缀构成，语义偏移为性质描述）
现实地；写实地（由前一个形容词加构成副词的后缀构成，语义偏移为方式）
现实；真实（由基础词加表示状态的后缀构成，语义偏移为「真实的状态」）

senses.title: Art that shows ordinary life
senses.titleCN: 描绘日常生活的现实主义
senses.definition: a nineteenth-century art movement that depicted ordinary people and everyday scenes without idealising them
senses.definitionCN: 十九世纪一场描绘普通人和平常场景、不作美化的艺术运动
senses.example: The painter recorded the bakery's worn sign with realism.
senses.exampleCN: 画家用写实手法画下面包店的旧招牌。
senses.why: The word claims that the artwork corresponds to the thing itself. Ordinary life is chosen because it has not been arranged for display.
senses.whyCN: 这个词主张作品与事物本身相对应。选择日常生活，是因为它没有被安排成展示的样子。

senses.title: Literary realism
senses.definition: a style of fiction that presents plausible people, settings and causes without romantic exaggeration
senses.definitionCN: 以可信的人物、环境与因果呈现生活、不作浪漫夸张的小说风格
senses.example: The novel brought realism to the industrial city.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说把现实主义带进工业城市。
senses.why: Fiction can either flatter life or report it. Realism chooses report, and its plots follow ordinary cause and effect.
senses.whyCN: 小说可以美化生活，也可以报道生活。现实主义选择报道，情节遵循日常的因果关系。

senses.title: The quality of being true to life
senses.definition: the degree to which a work or account matches how things actually look or happen
senses.definitionCN: 作品或叙述与实际外观或实际发生相符的程度
senses.example: The film's realism comes from its unpolished streets.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片的真实感来自未经修饰的街道。
senses.why: Here the word is a measure rather than a movement: any detail that matches experience increases realism.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词是一种尺度，而不是一场运动：任何与经验相符的细节都增加真实感。

senses.title: A practical attitude
senses.definition: the habit of accepting facts and limits rather than wishes or ideals
senses.definitionCN: 接受事实与限制、而非愿望或理想的态度
senses.example: The plan was received with realism rather than hope.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划得到的是务实评估，而非乐观期待。
senses.why: Someone who sees things as they are will not promise what cannot be done. The art sense becomes a temperament.
senses.whyCN: 看清事物本相的人不会承诺做不到的事。艺术义由此变成一种性情。

senses.title: Philosophical realism
senses.definition: the view that reality, or universals, exists independently of how minds perceive or describe it
senses.definitionCN: 认为实在或共相独立于心灵感知与描述而存在的观点
senses.example: Realism holds that the mountain exists before anyone climbs it.
senses.exampleCN: 实在论认为山在有人攀登之前就已存在。
senses.why: Philosophy asks whether the world depends on the observer. Realism answers no, and that answer is the oldest sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 哲学追问世界是否依赖观察者。实在论回答「不」，这个回答正是这个词最古老的义项。

senses.title: Realism in international relations
senses.titleCN: 国际关系中的现实主义
senses.definition: the theory that states act mainly to pursue power and security in an anarchic world
senses.definitionCN: 认为国家在无政府的世界上主要追求权力与安全的理论
senses.example: Realism explains the alliance as a balance of power.
senses.exampleCN: 现实主义把这个联盟解释为权力平衡。
senses.why: Political realism applies the practical attitude to states: it assumes interests, not ideals, drive decisions.
senses.whyCN: 政治现实主义把务实态度用到国家上：它假定驱动决策的是利益，而非理想。

senses.title: Legal realism
senses.definition: the view that law is what courts and officials actually do rather than only what statutes say
senses.definitionCN: 认为法律在于法院与官员实际怎么做、而不只是条文怎么写的主张
senses.example: Legal realism studies how judges really decide cases.
senses.exampleCN: 法律现实主义研究法官实际如何判案。
senses.why: The same move recurs: look at practice rather than at the official description. Law's realism is about what happens in court.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动作反复出现：看实践，而不是看官方描述。法学的现实主义关注的是法庭里实际发生的事。

senses.title: Photographic and cinematic realism
senses.definition: the impression that a photograph or film shows events as they occurred, without intervention
senses.definitionCN: 照片或影片呈现事件如同自然发生、未经干预的印象
senses.example: Handheld camera work adds realism to the scene.
senses.exampleCN: 手持摄影给这个场景增添了真实感。
senses.why: A camera seems to record rather than compose, so its images borrow the word for truth even though every frame is chosen.
senses.whyCN: 摄影机看似记录而非构图，因此它的影像借用了表示「真实」的词，尽管每一帧都是被选定的。

senses.title: Socialist realism
senses.definition: the official style required in Soviet art, showing workers and leaders in an idealised revolutionary light
senses.definitionCN: 苏联艺术中被要求采用的官方风格，以理想化的革命光辉表现劳动者与领袖
senses.example: Socialist realism turned factory work into heroic painting.
senses.exampleCN: 社会主义现实主义把工厂劳动变成英雄式绘画。
senses.why: The name is paradoxical: a style called realism by decree idealises its subjects. The word here marks political approval, not accuracy.
senses.whyCN: 这个名称本身矛盾：一种被法令规定为现实主义的风格却在美化对象。此处这个词标记的是政治认可，而非准确。

intro.en: Realism is Latin 'thing' plus the Greek suffix for a system or practice. The philosophical use is oldest, while the artistic use dates from the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: realism 由拉丁语表示「事物」的词加上表示体系或做法的希腊后缀构成。哲学用法最古老，艺术用法则始于十九世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin res meant 'thing, matter, affair'. Its deeper origin is source uncertain, and any older root proposed for it is a reconstructed form.
items.cn: 拉丁 res 意为「事物、事情、要务」。其更深来源属「来源不确定」，为其提出的更早词根都是重构形式。

items.en: Late Latin realis 'of a thing' produced the English adjective real, first in the sense of something that actually exists.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 realis「关于事物的」产生英语形容词 real，最初指确实存在的东西。

items.en: The suffix -ism came through Latin from Greek -ismos, naming a practice, system or doctrine.
items.cn: 表示学说的后缀经拉丁语来自希腊同名后缀，用来命名一种做法、体系或学说。

items.en: In medieval philosophy realism named the view that universals are real; nominalism was its opposite. This use predates the artistic one.
items.cn: 在中世纪哲学中，realism 指认为共相真实存在的观点，唯名论则是其对立面。这一用法早于艺术用法。

items.en: French criticism used réalisme in the nineteenth century for painters and novelists who reported ordinary life, and English followed.
items.cn: 法国批评界在十九世纪用 réalisme 指报道日常生活的画家与小说家，英语随后跟进。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of res is unresolved, and older Indo-European forms offered for it are reconstructed forms rather than recorded words.
items.cn: 来源不确定：res 在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，为其提出的更早印欧语形式属于重构形式，而非有记录的真实词形。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same stem that are constantly confused; group two holds competing ways of describing truth to life.
note.cn: 第一组是同出一个词干、极易混淆的词；第二组是描述「贴近生活」的几种竞争性说法。

entries.definition: a person who holds the view, or an adjective describing that style; realism is the view itself.
entries.definitionCN: 持这种观点的人，或描述这种风格的形容词；realism 是观点本身。

entries.definition: sensible and true to life; it describes things, while realism names a movement or doctrine.
entries.definitionCN: 合理且贴近现实的；它描述事物，而 realism 指运动或学说。

entries.definition: what actually exists; realism is the attitude or style that respects it.
entries.definitionCN: 实际存在的事物；realism 是尊重它的态度或风格。

entries.definition: land and buildings as property; it comes from real in the legal sense of immovable property, not from realism.
entries.definitionCN: 作为财产的土地与建筑；它来自 real 表示「不动产」的法律义，与 realism 无关。

entries.definition: a style that applies an almost scientific observation of cause and environment; it is stricter and often darker than realism.
entries.definitionCN: 近乎科学地观察因果与环境的一种风格；比现实主义更严格，也常更阴暗。

entries.definition: the deliberate choice of ugly or ordinary detail for maximum accuracy; it pushes realism to an extreme.
entries.definitionCN: 刻意选择丑陋或平常的细节以求最大准确；把现实主义推到极端。

entries.definition: the doctrine that the worth of an idea lies in its practical results; it shares realism's practical temper but is a philosophy of action.
entries.definitionCN: 认为观念的价值在于实际结果的主张；与现实主义共享务实气质，但它是行动哲学。

entries.definition: the view that reality is mental, or the habit of measuring life against ideals; it is the standing opposite of realism in both art and philosophy.
entries.definitionCN: 认为实在是精神的，或以理想衡量生活的习惯；在艺术与哲学中都是现实主义的对立面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Realism is real plus -ism: the doctrine or practice of the thing itself.
normal.cn: realism 是在 real 之后加表示学说的后缀：关于事物本身的做法或学说。

normal.en: The philosophical sense is older than the artistic one, which is why the word also means a belief about reality.
normal.cn: 哲学义比艺术义更古老，所以这个词也指一种关于实在的信念。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its branches: literary, socialist, magical, political.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出它的分支：文学的、社会主义的、魔幻的、政治的。

normal.en: A realist is the person; realistic is the adjective; realism is the position.
normal.cn: realist 指人；realistic 是形容词；realism 是立场。

normal.en: The stem res means 'thing', so realism always turns attention back to things.
normal.cn: 词干 res 意为「事物」，所以 realism 总是把注意力转回事物本身。

abstract.en: Picture a painter refusing to move a chair because the room looks better without it.
abstract.cn: 想象一位画家拒绝挪动椅子，因为房间没有它更好看。

abstract.en: Picture a mountain that keeps existing when nobody is looking at it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座山，在无人观看时仍然存在。

abstract.en: Picture a style ordered by the state to call itself truthful.
abstract.cn: 想象一种被国家要求自称真实的风格。

examples.en: Realism in painting began with scenes of work and poverty.
examples.cn: 绘画中的现实主义从劳动与贫困的场景开始。

examples.en: The report was written with realism about the budget.
examples.cn: 这份报告对预算作了务实的评估。

examples.en: Philosophical realism defends a world independent of our descriptions.
examples.cn: 哲学实在论捍卫一个独立于我们描述的世界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「真实 + 主义」—— 坚持照着事物本来的样子写和画 → 现实主义、写实主义

root: 由晚期拉丁 realis「关于事物的」加希腊系的学说后缀构成；realis 出自拉丁 res「事物」。res 在拉丁语之前的来源不确定，更早的印欧语形式均属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one demand: look at the thing itself. Art, fiction, photography and law apply it to seeing and recording, while practical life, philosophy and politics apply it to belief and decision.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围绕同一个要求展开：看事物本身。艺术、小说、摄影与法律把它用于观看与记录，务实生活、哲学与政治则把它用于信念与决策。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand recording exactly what is on the table, including the dirt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把桌上的东西原样记下，连灰尘也不漏。

branches.en: ART AND FICTION: painting and the novel report ordinary life instead of improving it.
branches.cn: 艺术与小说：绘画与小说报道日常生活，而不是美化它。

branches.en: MEASURE OF TRUTH: a detail or a camera image can be judged by how closely it matches experience.
branches.cn: 真实尺度：细节或摄影影像可按其与经验的接近程度来评判。

branches.en: TEMPERAMENT: the same demand becomes a practical attitude toward limits.
branches.cn: 性情：同一个要求变成面对限制时的务实态度。

branches.en: TWO POLES: philosophy asserts an independent world, while socialist realism shows a doctrine using the word for approval.
branches.cn: 两极：哲学主张独立世界，社会主义现实主义则展示一种学说如何借这个词表示认可。

branches.en: PRACTICE OVER THEORY: politics and law study what actors actually do.
branches.cn: 实践重于理论：政治与法学研究行动者实际做了什么。

intro.en: Realism is one branch of the large real- family, built on a Latin word for 'thing' and expanded by a suffix for doctrines.
intro.cn: realism 是庞大的 real- 词族中的一支，其核心是拉丁语表示「事物」的词，再由表示学说的后缀扩展而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin res 'thing' gives realis and realitas; English builds real, reality, realize, realism, realist and realistic on that stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 res「事物」给出 realis 与 realitas；英语在这一词干上构成 real、reality、realize、realism、realist 与 realistic。

items.example: Res is the stem behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: res 是整个词族背后的词干。

items.example: Realis produced English real.
items.exampleCN: realis 产生英语 real。

items.example: The real chair stood in the corner.
items.exampleCN: 那把真椅子就放在角落里。

items.example: Realism names a doctrine about things.
items.exampleCN: realism 命名一种关于事物的学说。

items.meaning: the doctrine or style of things as they are
items.meaningCN: 照事物本相的主张或风格
items.example: Realism dominated the gallery.
items.exampleCN: 现实主义占据了画廊。

items.meaning: a believer in or maker of realism
items.meaningCN: 现实主义者；写实创作者
items.example: The realist chose a factory gate.
items.exampleCN: 这位写实画家选择了工厂大门。

items.example: The estimate was realistic.
items.exampleCN: 这个估算是合乎实际的。

items.example: Reality resisted the plan.
items.exampleCN: 现实让计划受挫。

items.example: They realized the design in stone.
items.exampleCN: 他们用石头实现了这个设计。

items.example: The light made the street unreal.
items.exampleCN: 那种光让街道显得不真实。

definition_zh: adj. 不对称的（两侧形状不同）；（关系、信息、力量）不对等的
definition_en: Having two halves that differ in shape or size; of a relationship, unevenly balanced in information, power or obligation.
core_image: 一件衣服左右两片长短不一，天平一头明显下沉
scene: 这件外套左右长短不同，是刻意剪成这样的。 The coat has an asymmetric cut, longer on one side.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：asymmetric 指两侧形状或大小不同，即不对称。

pos.zh: 不对称的；不对等的

senses.title: Unequal in shape
senses.definition: having sides or halves that do not match in shape, size or placement
senses.definitionCN: 两侧或两半在形状、大小或位置上不相配
senses.example: The facade is deliberately asymmetric.
senses.exampleCN: 这个立面是故意做成不对称的。
senses.why: The root means measure, and the prefix removes it, so the word says the two sides cannot be measured alike.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「量度」，前缀把它取消，所以这个词说的是两侧无法用同一尺度量出相同结果。

senses.title: Unequal in a relationship
senses.definition: of information, power or duty, distributed unevenly between the parties involved
senses.definitionCN: 指信息、权力或义务在各方之间分布不均
senses.example: The market fails when information is asymmetric.
senses.exampleCN: 信息不对称时市场就会失灵。
senses.why: Economics borrowed the shape word for balance, because a lopsided scale is the oldest picture of unfairness.
senses.whyCN: 经济学借用了这个形状词来讲「均衡」，因为一头下沉的天平是关于不公最古老的画面。

intro.en: Asymmetric is Greek asymmetros, from a-, without, and symmetria, from syn-, together, and metron, measure: not measuring together.
intro.cn: asymmetric 就是希腊语 asymmetros，由 a-「无」与 symmetria 构成，后者出自 syn-「共同」加 metron「量度」：不能共同量出同一结果。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to measure lies behind metre, measure and geometry alike.
items.cn: 一个意为「量」的拟构词根同时藏在 metre、measure 与 geometry 背后。

items.en: Greek metron meant a measure or a rule for measuring, the core of the whole family.
items.cn: 希腊语 metron 意为「量度、量尺」，是整个词族的核心。

items.en: With syn-, together, symmetria meant measuring together, hence proportion and balanced form.
items.cn: 加上 syn-「共同」后，symmetria 意为「共同量度」，因而指比例与匀称。

items.en: The prefix a- negated it, giving asymmetros, without common measure.
items.cn: 前缀 a- 加以否定，得到 asymmetros「没有共同量度」。

items.en: English formed asymmetric in the eighteenth century as geometry and design demanded the term.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪构成 asymmetric，因为几何与设计需要这个术语。

items.en: Twentieth-century economics and strategy applied it to information and power, giving the second sense.
items.cn: 二十世纪经济学与战略学把它用于信息与权力，产生第二个义项。

note.en: The look-alike group is the whole measure family with and without the negative prefix; the near-meaning group lists everyday words for lopsidedness.
note.cn: 形近组是带与不带否定前缀的整个「量度」词族；近义组列出日常表示「一边偏」的词。

entries.definition: Having matching halves.
entries.definitionCN: 两半相配的。

entries.definition: The absence of symmetry.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏对称。

entries.definition: Relating to shapes and their measures.
entries.definitionCN: 与形状及其量度有关的。

entries.definition: Relating to measurement or a system of it.
entries.definitionCN: 与测量或度量制有关的。

entries.definition: Heavier or lower on one side.
entries.definitionCN: 一侧更重或更低。

entries.definition: Not level, smooth or balanced.
entries.definitionCN: 不平、不匀或不均衡。

entries.definition: Lacking equal weight or stability.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏均等的分量或稳定。

entries.definition: Favouring one side only.
entries.definitionCN: 只偏向一方。

normalIntro.en: Asymmetric is a-, not, plus sym-, together, plus metric, measure: the two sides do not measure the same.
normalIntro.cn: asymmetric 就是 a-「不」加 sym-「共同」加 metric「量度」：两侧量不出同一个结果。

normal.en: Asymmetric and asymmetrical are both correct.
normal.cn: asymmetric 与 asymmetrical 都对。

normal.en: Asymmetry is the noun, asymmetrically the adverb.
normal.cn: asymmetry 是名词，asymmetrically 是副词。

normal.en: Symmetric is the same word without the negative.
normal.cn: symmetric 就是去掉否定的同一个词。

normal.en: Asymmetric information is a set economics phrase.
normal.cn: asymmetric information 是经济学固定说法。

normal.en: Lopsided is the everyday substitute.
normal.cn: lopsided 是日常替换词。

abstract.en: Picture a coat longer on the left than the right.
abstract.cn: 想象一件左边比右边长的外套。

abstract.en: Imagine a scale with one pan clearly lower.
abstract.cn: 想象一头明显下沉的天平。

abstract.en: Think of one side knowing what the other cannot.
abstract.cn: 想象一方知道另一方无从知道的事。

examples.en: The garden follows an asymmetric plan.
examples.cn: 这座花园采用不对称的布局。

examples.en: Asymmetric power breeds resentment.
examples.cn: 权力不对等会滋生怨恨。

examples.en: Her smile was slightly asymmetric.
examples.cn: 她的笑略微不对称。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：a-「不」+ sym「共同」+ metric「量度」——两边量不到一块儿，就是不对称 asymmetric。

root: 希腊语 metron「量度」加 syn-「共同」构成 symmetria「匀称」，再加否定前缀 a- 成 asymmetros；英语十八世纪造 asymmetric，二十世纪扩用于信息与权力。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses deny a common measure: two halves that will not match, and two parties who do not hold the same weight.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都否认「共同量度」：无法相配的两半，以及分量不同的两方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one side longer, one pan of the scale clearly lower
core.cn: 核心意象：一件衣服左右两片长短不一，天平一头明显下沉

branches.cn: 一侧更长的外套。

branches.cn: 两侧之间没有共同的量度。
