definition_zh: 食草动物；植食动物
definition_en: an animal that feeds chiefly on plants, including grasses, leaves, fruits, seeds and sometimes algae
core_image: 一头牛低头啃食草甸，嘴角挂着草屑，身后的草地被啃出一道道弧线
scene: 这里指「食草动物」。 The deer is a browser herbivore that strips leaves from shrubs rather than grazing the open meadow.
sceneCN: 这里 herbivore 指「植食动物」（第 1 个义项：以植物为主要食物）；这种鹿是啃食灌木枝叶的植食动物，而不是在开阔草地上放牧。图中可辨识物件：牛、草甸、灌木枝叶、被啃出的弧线。

pos.zh: 食草动物；植食动物（可数，复数 herbivores）

collocations.zh: 放牧型植食动物；吃草类
啃食型植食动物；吃枝叶类
专性植食动物；必须吃植物才能存活
植食诱导防御；植物因被啃食而产生的化学防御

senses.title: An animal that eats plants
senses.titleCN: 植食动物：以植物为主要食物
senses.definition: an animal whose diet consists mainly of plant material such as grass, leaves, fruit or seeds
senses.definitionCN: 指以草、叶、果实或种子等植物材料为主要食物的动物
senses.example: The savanna supports herds of large herbivores during the wet season.
senses.exampleCN: 雨季时，稀树草原养活了成群的巨型植食动物。
senses.why: The word names a dietary class by its food source, so the definition is about what enters the mouth, not about teeth or hooves.
senses.whyCN: 这个词按食物来源命名食性类别，定义关注的是吃进嘴里的东西，而不是牙齿或蹄子。

senses.title: Grazers and browsers
senses.titleCN: 放牧型与啃食型：两种取食方式
senses.definition: a herbivore classified by feeding style, either cropping grass low to the ground or stripping leaves and twigs from shrubs and trees
senses.definitionCN: 指按取食方式分类的植食动物：或贴地啃食草类，或摘取灌木与树木的枝叶
senses.example: Grazing herbivores keep the grassland short, while browsing herbivores reach into the canopy.
senses.exampleCN: 放牧型植食动物把草地压短，啃食型则伸进树冠取食。
senses.why: Ecology splits the class by height of feeding, because grass and browse regrow differently under the same animal pressure.
senses.whyCN: 生态学按取食高度细分这一类，因为草与枝叶在同样取食压力下再生方式不同。

senses.title: Gut and fermentation
senses.titleCN: 消化道与发酵：靠微生物分解纤维素
senses.definition: a herbivore defined by its digestive arrangement, such as a rumen or a hindgut, where microbes break down cellulose
senses.definitionCN: 指按消化结构界定的植食动物，如具有瘤胃或后肠，由微生物分解纤维素
senses.example: As a ruminant herbivore, the cow relies on rumen microbes to digest grass.
senses.exampleCN: 作为反刍型植食动物，牛依靠瘤胃微生物消化草料。
senses.why: Plants are tough, so herbivores are defined as much by the microbial partnership in their gut as by their food.
senses.whyCN: 植物很坚韧，因此植食动物既由食物界定，也同样由肠道中的微生物伙伴界定。

senses.title: Obligate versus facultative
senses.titleCN: 专性与兼性：能否靠植物独活
senses.definition: a herbivore that must eat plants to survive, as opposed to one that eats plants only when other food is scarce
senses.definitionCN: 指必须吃植物才能存活的植食动物，与仅在其他食物稀缺时才吃植物的兼性者相对
senses.example: The koala is an obligate herbivore restricted to a few eucalypt species.
senses.exampleCN: 考拉是专性植食动物，只吃少数几种桉树。
senses.why: The distinction separates a fixed diet from an opportunistic one, which matters when habitats change.
senses.whyCN: 这一区分把固定食性与机会性食性分开，在生境变化时尤为重要。

senses.title: Herbivore as ecosystem engineer
senses.titleCN: 生态系统工程师：植食动物塑造植被
senses.definition: a herbivore whose feeding and trampling reshape plant communities and therefore the habitats of other species
senses.definitionCN: 指其取食与踩踏重塑植物群落、进而改变其他物种生境的植食动物
senses.example: The elephant is a herbivore that engineers the savanna by pushing over trees.
senses.exampleCN: 大象是一种植食动物，它推倒树木，从而改造稀树草原。
senses.why: The label stops describing a diet and starts describing a force: what the animal eats determines what everyone else can eat.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签不再只描述食性，而开始描述一种力量：它吃什么决定了别人能吃什么。

senses.title: Plant defence against herbivores
senses.titleCN: 植物的防御：针对植食动物的化学与物理屏障
senses.definition: the role of a herbivore as the pressure that selects for thorns, toxins and tough tissues in plants
senses.definitionCN: 指植食动物作为选择压力，促使植物演化出刺、毒素与坚韧组织的角色
senses.example: Thorns and bitter alkaloids are defences aimed at herbivores.
senses.exampleCN: 刺与苦味生物碱是针对植食动物的防御。
senses.why: The word appears on the attacking side of a coevolutionary arms race, which is why plant defences are named after it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出现在共同演化军备竞赛的进攻一方，因此植物的防御以它为名。

senses.title: Marine herbivores
senses.titleCN: 海洋植食者：海草与藻类的取食者
senses.definition: an aquatic animal that feeds on seagrass, algae or other marine plants
senses.definitionCN: 指以海草、藻类或其他海洋植物为食的水生动物
senses.example: Sea turtles and some reef fish are marine herbivores that keep algae short.
senses.exampleCN: 海龟与部分礁鱼是海洋植食者，它们把藻类压短。
senses.why: The class crosses the shoreline: wherever there is plant tissue, there is a herbivore adapted to eat it.
senses.whyCN: 这一类跨越海岸线：凡有植物组织的地方，就有适应取食它的植食动物。

senses.title: Herbivore in casual speech
senses.titleCN: 口语用法：素食者或食性比喻
senses.definition: an informal or humorous use for a person who eats a plant-based diet, or for a mild, non-aggressive party
senses.definitionCN: 口语或戏谑用法，指以植物性饮食为主的人，或指温和不具攻击性的一方
senses.example: He calls himself a herbivore, though he still eats eggs.
senses.exampleCN: 他自称植食者，不过仍然吃蛋。
senses.why: The zoological word has drifted into diet talk, where it is friendlier and less doctrinal than vegetarian.
senses.whyCN: 这个动物学词汇漂移到饮食话题，在那里比「素食者」这一说法更轻松、更少教条色彩。

intro.en: Herbivore is a modern scientific compound from Latin herba 'grass, herb' and vorare 'to devour', literally 'plant devourer'.
intro.cn: herbivore 是近代科学复合词，由拉丁语 herba「草、草本」与 vorare「吞食」构成，字面即「吞食植物者」。

items.en: Herba meant grass, green plants or an herb, and it also underlies herb, herbage and herbaceous in English.
items.cn: herba 指草、绿色植物或香草，也是英语 herb、herbage、herbaceous 的来源。

items.en: Vorare meant to devour or swallow whole. It is the second half of carnivore, omnivore, insectivore and voracious.
items.cn: vorare 意为吞食、整口吞下，它是 carnivore、omnivore、insectivore 与 voracious 的后半部分。

items.en: The compound was formed in modern scientific Latin, and French zoologist Georges Cuvier is usually credited with popularising the dietary classification in the early nineteenth century. The exact coining is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个复合词在近代科学拉丁语中形成；一般认为法国动物学家居维叶在 19 世纪早期推广了这套食性分类，但确切的造词者存疑。

items.en: Zoology standardised the triad herbivore, carnivore and omnivore, turning a descriptive compound into a classification system.
items.cn: 动物学把 herbivore、carnivore、omnivore 确立为三分法，把一个描述性复合词变成分类体系。

items.en: The pattern later produced insectivore, frugivore, folivore and nectarivore, each naming a specific plant or animal food.
items.cn: 这一模式后来派生出 insectivore、frugivore、folivore、nectarivore，各自命名特定的植物或动物食物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -vore ending and must be told apart by the first element; the near-meaning group separates diet class from feeding style.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -vore 结尾，须靠前半部分区分；近义组区分食性类别与取食方式。

entries.definition: An animal that eats mainly animal flesh. The first element is Latin caro 'flesh', so the two words differ at the stem, not the ending.
entries.definitionCN: 指以动物肉为主食的动物。前半是拉丁语 caro「肉」，因此两词区别在词干而非词尾。

entries.definition: An animal that eats both plant and animal food. The first element omni- 'all' marks the broader diet.
entries.definitionCN: 指既吃植物也吃动物的动物。前半 omni-「全部」标出更宽的食性。

entries.definition: The adjective form meaning plant-eating. Herbivore is the noun for the animal, so the two cannot swap places.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词形式，意为植食的。herbivore 是动物的名词，两者不能互换位置。

entries.definition: A herbivore that crops grass and low vegetation. It is a subset of herbivore, defined by feeding height rather than diet alone.
entries.definitionCN: 指啃食草类与低矮植被的植食动物。它是植食动物的子集，按取食高度而非仅按食性界定。

entries.definition: A herbivore that strips leaves and twigs from shrubs and trees. Do not confuse it with the web browser.
entries.definitionCN: 指摘食灌木与树木枝叶的植食动物。注意不要与网络浏览器混淆。

entries.definition: A herbivore specialising in leaves. It is narrower than herbivore, which also covers grass, fruit and seed eaters.
entries.definitionCN: 指专食树叶的植食动物，比 herbivore 更窄，后者还包括吃草、果实与种子者。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: herba 'grass' + vorare 'devour': the plant devourer.
normal.cn: herba「草」+ vorare「吞食」：吞食植物者。

normal.en: Read -vore as 'eater' and the first half names the food: herbi-, carni-, omni-, insecti-.
normal.cn: 把 -vore 读作「吃……者」，前半部分就是食物：herbi-、carni-、omni-、insecti-。

normal.en: The family runs herb, herbaceous, herbage, herbicide, herbivorous and herbivory.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 herb、herbaceous、herbage、herbicide、herbivorous、herbivory。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: grazing herbivore, browsing herbivore, obligate herbivore, herbivore population.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：放牧型植食动物、啃食型植食动物、专性植食动物、植食动物种群。

normal.en: Cuvier is usually credited with the dietary triad in the early 1800s, though the coining is uncertain.
normal.cn: 一般认为居维叶在 1800 年代初提出这套食性三分法，但造词者存疑。

abstract.en: Picture a cow tearing grass with a sideways sweep of its head.
abstract.cn: 想象一头牛把头一甩，撕下一把草。

abstract.en: Picture a deer standing on hind legs to reach leaves above the browse line.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鹿立起后腿，够取啃食线以上的树叶。

abstract.en: Picture an elephant pushing a tree over so the whole herd can feed.
abstract.cn: 想象大象推倒一棵树，让整群都能取食。

examples.en: Large herbivores keep the savanna open by eating young trees.
examples.cn: 大型植食动物吃掉落树幼苗，使稀树草原保持开阔。

examples.en: The koala is an obligate herbivore with a narrow diet.
examples.cn: 考拉是食性很窄的专性植食动物。

examples.en: Plant toxins evolved as defences against herbivores.
examples.cn: 植物毒素是作为抵御植食动物的防御演化出来的。

dict_mnemonic.text: herb（草本）+ vore（吃……者）→ 吃草的东西 → herbivore 食草动物

root: 拉丁 herba「草、草本」+ vorare「吞食」→ 近代科学拉丁语 herbivorus／herbivore「吞食植物者」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the plain diet label and then add feeding height, gut design, obligation, ecosystem effects, plant defence, marine life and casual speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从最朴素的食性标签开始，再依次加入取食高度、消化道设计、专性程度、生态效应、植物防御、海洋生活与口语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cow sweeping grass into its mouth, leaving curved bite marks.
core.cn: 核心意象：牛把草扫进嘴里，留下弧形咬痕。

branches.en: DIET: the base sense names an animal by what it eats.
branches.cn: 食性：基本义按吃什么来命名动物。

branches.en: STYLE: grazer and browser split the class by feeding height.
branches.cn: 方式：放牧型与啃食型按取食高度细分这一类。

branches.en: PHYSIOLOGY AND NECESSITY: gut microbes and obligation decide whether plants can be the only food.
branches.cn: 生理与必要性：肠道微生物与专性程度决定植物能否成为唯一食物。

branches.en: FORCE: the herbivore shapes plant communities, and plants evolve defences against it.
branches.cn: 力量：植食动物塑造植物群落，植物则演化出针对它的防御。

branches.en: RANGE: the label crosses into the sea and into casual talk about diets.
branches.cn: 范围：这个标签跨入海洋，也跨入口语中的饮食话题。

intro.en: Herbivore is a two-part scientific compound, and the same -vore ending builds a whole family of diet words.
intro.cn: herbivore 是两部分构成的科学复合词，同一个 -vore 结尾还能造出一整族食性词汇。

latinIntro.en: Herba supplies the food, vorare supplies the eating, and the compound was fixed in modern scientific Latin before entering English.
latinIntro.cn: herba 提供食物，vorare 提供吃，这个复合词在近代科学拉丁语中定型后才进入英语。

items.meaningCN: 用于食物、药物或调味的植物
items.example: The garden grows culinary herbs.

items.example: The border is planted with herbaceous perennials.
items.exampleCN: 花境里种的是草本多年生植物。

items.example: The field was cleared with herbicide.
items.exampleCN: 这块田用除草剂清除了杂草。

items.example: The carnivore hunts at dusk.

items.meaning: animal eating both plants and flesh
items.meaningCN: 既吃植物也吃肉的动物

intro.en: Decrepit comes from Latin decrepitus, broken down by age, from de- plus crepare, to crack.
intro.cn: decrepit 源自拉丁语 decrepitus（因年老而衰败），由 de- 加 crepare（裂开、作响）构成。

items.en: Crepare meant to crack or rattle.
items.cn: crepare 意为裂开或作响。

items.en: Decrepitus described someone broken by age.
items.cn: decrepitus 形容被岁月压垮的人。

items.en: Decrepite was an early English spelling.
items.cn: decrepite 是早期英语拼法。

items.en: Decrepit settled as the modern spelling.
items.cn: 十六世纪 decrepit 定为现代拼法。

items.en: Decrepit was used for buildings and machines.

items.en: Decrepit became common in urban reporting.

entries.definition: Becoming gradually worse or rotten.

entries.definition: Damaged or thin from long use.
entries.definitionCN: 磨损的；用旧的。

definition_zh: 品牌知名度；品牌认知度
definition_en: the extent to which buyers know that a brand exists and can recognize or recall it
core_image: 一排货架前，顾客还没走近就先用手指向其中一个盒子，因为他早就认得那个名字
scene: 货架前，顾客还没走近就用手指向其中一个盒子，因为他早就认得那个名字。 Brand awareness rose sharply after the stadium took the company's name.
sceneCN: 货架前，顾客还没走近就用手指向其中一个盒子，因为他早就认得那个名字；句中的这个短语指「买家对某品牌存在与识别的知晓程度」（第 1 个义项：能认出该品牌、且知道它存在的那部分人群比例）。图中可辨识物件：货架、指向的手指、盒子、体育场冠名牌、调查问卷。

pos.zh: 品牌知名度（不可数）
品牌认知度；品牌知晓（营销术语，不可数）

forms.label: 复数（少见，指多次测量结果）

senses.title: Buyers know the brand exists
senses.titleCN: 品牌知名度：知道它存在
senses.definition: the share of buyers who know that a brand exists and can recognize it
senses.definitionCN: 知道某品牌存在并能认出它的买家所占的比例
senses.example: Brand awareness rose sharply after the stadium took the company's name.
senses.exampleCN: 体育场冠上公司名字后，品牌知名度大幅上升。
senses.why: Awareness is a state of knowing, and a brand's first task is to be known at all before it can be preferred.
senses.whyCN: awareness 是「知道」的状态，而一个品牌的第一件事，是在被偏好之前先被人知道。

senses.title: Buyers know what the brand does
senses.titleCN: 品牌认知：知道它是做什么的
senses.definition: the level of understanding buyers have about what the brand sells or stands for
senses.definitionCN: 买家对该品牌卖什么、代表什么的理解程度
senses.example: Awareness was high, but few knew the brand made tools rather than toys.
senses.exampleCN: 知名度很高，但很少有人知道这个品牌做的是工具而不是玩具。
senses.why: Knowing a name is not knowing a meaning; the second step fills the name with content.
senses.whyCN: 知道一个名字不等于知道它的含义；第二步是往这个名字里填内容。

senses.title: The brand comes to mind unprompted
senses.definition: the state in which buyers name the brand themselves when a product category is mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 当提到某个品类时，买家自己就能说出该品牌的状态
senses.example: Top-of-mind awareness is what every launch really wants.
senses.exampleCN: 无提示的第一联想，才是每次上市真正想要的。
senses.why: This is awareness at its strongest: no cue is needed, so the name sits at the front of memory.
senses.whyCN: 这是最强程度的知晓：不需要任何提示，名字就坐在记忆最前面。

senses.title: The brand is recognized when shown
senses.definition: the state in which buyers recognize the brand once its name or logo is shown
senses.definitionCN: 一旦看到名字或标识，买家就能认出该品牌的状态
senses.example: Aided awareness was ninety per cent, unaided only twelve.
senses.exampleCN: 提示后的识别率是九成，无提示的只有一成二。
senses.why: Recognition is the weaker form: a cue does half the work, and the memory only has to agree.
senses.whyCN: 识别是较弱的一种：提示做了一半的活，记忆只需点头。

senses.title: The brand is recalled at the moment of buying
senses.definition: the state in which the brand occurs to a buyer while choosing in a shop or a feed
senses.definitionCN: 买家在店里或信息流里挑选时想到该品牌的状态
senses.example: Awareness without availability does not survive the walk down the aisle.
senses.exampleCN: 只有知名度而买不到，走不到货架尽头就消失了。
senses.why: Memory must fire at the moment of choice, or the name is known and useless.
senses.whyCN: 记忆必须在选择的瞬间被点亮，否则这个名字虽被知道却毫无用处。

senses.title: Awareness produced by advertising
senses.definition: the level of knowing that paid messages have created in a population
senses.definitionCN: 付费信息在一群人身上造出的知晓程度
senses.example: The campaign lifted awareness among teenagers by a third.
senses.exampleCN: 这场宣传把青少年中的知晓度提高了三分之一。
senses.why: Advertising buys attention, and awareness is the residue that attention leaves behind.
senses.whyCN: 广告买注意力，而知晓度就是注意力留下的残留物。

senses.title: A measured marketing figure
senses.titleCN: 调研指标：可量化的知名度
senses.definition: a numeric indicator reported in market research, usually as a percentage of a group
senses.definitionCN: 市场调研中汇报的数值指标，通常以某人群的百分比表示
senses.example: The report tracks awareness quarterly against three rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告每季度追踪与三家对手相比的知名度。
senses.why: Once a state of mind is worth money, it gets counted, and the counted thing takes the name of the state.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某种心理状态值钱，它就会被计数，而被计数的那个东西就借用了这种状态的名字。

senses.title: The reach of exposure
senses.definition: the size of the audience that has been exposed to the brand's messages
senses.definitionCN: 接触过该品牌信息的人群规模
senses.example: Awareness of that size needs exposure of a size nobody budgeted for.
senses.exampleCN: 这样大的曝光度需要同样大的投放量，而没人为此做过预算。
senses.why: This is the input side: exposure measures who saw the message, awareness measures who kept it.
senses.whyCN: 这是输入一侧：曝光度衡量谁看到了信息，知晓度衡量谁把信息留了下来。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Germanic noun for a burned mark with an Old English adjective for being watchful. Both halves are old; the marketing use is recent.
intro.cn: 这个短语把日耳曼语里表示烙痕的名词，与古英语里表示「警觉、知道」的形容词连在一起。两半都很古老，营销用法却很新。

items.en: Brand meant 'fire, a burning piece of wood', then 'an ownership mark burned onto animals and goods'.
items.cn: brand 先指「火、燃烧的木块」，再指「烙在牲畜与货物上表示所有权的记号」。

items.en: Aware goes back to Old English gewær 'watchful, vigilant'. The same Germanic stock gives German gewahr 'aware'.
items.cn: aware 上溯到古英语 gewær「警觉的、留神的」。同一日耳曼词源给了德语 gewahr「知晓的」。

items.en: It is generally considered related to a reconstructed root meaning 'to perceive, to watch out for'. The reconstruction is standard, though the exact path is not demonstrated.
items.cn: 一般认为它与一个重构的「察觉、提防」词根相关。这一重构是通行说法，但确切路径未被证明。

items.en: The noun awareness is recorded in the nineteenth century, formed from aware plus -ness, meaning simply the state of knowing.
items.cn: 名词 awareness 在十九世纪有记录，由 aware 加 -ness 构成，只表示「知道的状态」。

items.en: Market research borrowed the word to measure whether buyers could name or recognize a brand, and split it into aided and unaided recall.
items.cn: 市场调研借走这个词，用来衡量买家能否说出或认出某个品牌，并把它分成提示回想与无提示回想。

items.en: Online advertising turned awareness into a continuous number, reported daily alongside clicks and impressions.
items.cn: 网络广告把知晓度变成一个连续更新的数字，与点击和曝光一起按日汇报。

note.en: Group one contains phrases built on the same two words; group two contains neighbouring marketing measures.
note.cn: 第一组由同样两个词构成；第二组是相邻的营销指标。

entries.definition: The ability to identify a brand when it is shown; it is the aided half, not the whole measure.
entries.definitionCN: 看到品牌标识时能认出来的能力；它只是提示的那一半，不是全部指标。

entries.definition: The ability to name a brand from memory without a cue; it is the harder and usually lower figure.
entries.definitionCN: 在没有提示时凭记忆说出品牌的能力；它更难，数值通常更低。

entries.definition: What buyers think the brand is like; awareness only asks whether they know it at all.
entries.definitionCN: 买家认为这个品牌是什么样子；awareness 只问他们是否知道它。

entries.definition: The habit of buying the same brand repeatedly; knowing a name does not imply buying it.
entries.definitionCN: 反复购买同一品牌的习惯；知道一个名字并不等于会买它。

entries.definition: How often a brand is seen, which is the input; awareness is what remains in the mind afterwards.
entries.definitionCN: 品牌被看见的频率，属于输入；awareness 是事后留在脑子里的东西。

entries.definition: A sense that a name is known and safe, often weaker and vaguer than measured awareness.
entries.definitionCN: 觉得这个名字熟悉、安全的感觉，往往比被测量的知晓度更弱、更模糊。

entries.definition: Attention gained, often unpaid; awareness is the knowledge that this attention leaves behind.
entries.definitionCN: 获得的关注，往往不付费；awareness 是这份关注留下的知识。

entries.definition: The number of different people exposed to a message; it counts exposure, not memory.
entries.definitionCN: 接触到某条信息的不同人数；它数的是曝光，不是记忆。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: two real words joined, and real research phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的词拼在一起，加上真实的研究说法。

normal.en: brand 'burned mark' + aware 'watchful': a mark people have noticed.
normal.cn: brand「烙痕」加 aware「留神的」：一个被人注意到的记号。

normal.en: Awareness splits into two halves in research: recognition with a cue, recall without one.
normal.cn: 在调研里，知晓度分成两半：有提示的识别，无提示的回想。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the trade: raise brand awareness, a brand awareness campaign, top-of-mind awareness.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示行业说法：提升知名度、品牌认知宣传活动、最先想到的品牌。

normal.en: aware + -ness gives the plain noun awareness, the state of knowing.
normal.cn: aware 加 -ness 得到朴素名词 awareness，即「知道的状态」。

normal.en: The old word gewær survives in the German gewahr, still meaning aware.
normal.cn: 古老的 gewær 还活在德语 gewahr 里，仍表示「知晓的」。

abstract.en: Picture a finger rising before the shopper reaches the shelf: that finger is awareness.
abstract.cn: 想象顾客还没走到货架，手指就先抬了起来：那根手指就是知晓度。

abstract.en: Knowing a name and knowing what it means are two different depths of the same water.
abstract.cn: 知道一个名字与知道它的含义，是同一片水的两个深度。

abstract.en: Exposure is what enters the eye; awareness is what stays after the eye moves on.
abstract.cn: 曝光是进入眼睛的东西；知晓度是目光移开之后留下的东西。

examples.en: The company spent two years buying brand awareness before it sold a single unit.
examples.cn: 这家公司先花两年买知名度，才卖出第一件产品。

examples.en: Brand awareness among rural buyers is still under a fifth.
examples.cn: 农村买家中的品牌知名度仍不足五分之一。

examples.en: They measured brand awareness before and after the sponsorship.
examples.cn: 他们测量了赞助前后的品牌知名度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「布兰德-阿威尔尼斯」——布上烙的记号（布兰德）被人「阿威尔」地看在眼里 → 品牌知名度

root: brand（日耳曼语「火、烙痕」）+ awareness（aware「警觉的、知晓的」+ -ness），合指「一个记号被人知道的程度」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses climb a ladder of knowing: that the brand exists, what it means, that it comes to mind alone, that it is recognized when shown, that it is recalled at the shelf, that advertising produced it, that it can be counted, and that it depends on exposure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着「知道」的梯子往上：知道它存在、知道它意味着什么、不用提示就想到、看见时认得出、在货架前想得起、由广告造出、可以被计数，以及它取决于曝光。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger rising toward a shelf before the shopper even arrives.
core.cn: 核心意象：顾客还没走到，手指就先指向货架。

branches.en: TWO STRENGTHS OF KNOWING: recognizing with a cue is easier than knowing without one.
branches.cn: 两种强度的知道：有提示时认出来，比没有提示时知道要容易。

branches.en: CONTENT: a known name still has to be filled with meaning.
branches.cn: 内容：被知道的名字仍须填进含义。

branches.en: FIRE AT THE RIGHT MOMENT: coming to mind unprompted and coming to mind at the shelf are the same spark, one earlier and one later.
branches.cn: 在对的时刻点亮：不用提示就想到，与在货架前想到，是同一个火花，一个更早一个更晚。

branches.en: INPUT: advertising buys exposure, and exposure is the raw material of knowing.
branches.cn: 输入：广告买到曝光，而曝光是「知道」的原料。

branches.en: NUMBER: once knowing is valuable, it is counted and becomes a figure.
branches.cn: 数字：一旦「知道」值钱，它就被计数，变成一个数值。

intro.en: This phrase is two whole words joined: a Germanic noun with no Latin cognate, and an Old English adjective plus a native suffix.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个完整的词拼成：一个没有拉丁同源词的日耳曼名词，和一个古英语形容词加本土后缀。

latinIntro.en: Neither half has a Latin source. Brand is Germanic; aware goes back to Old English gewær. Latin expresses the same ideas as nota for a mark and cognoscere for knowing, but these are different words, not relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都没有拉丁来源。brand 属日耳曼语；aware 上溯古英语 gewær。拉丁语用 nota 表示记号、用 cognoscere 表示知道，但那是不同的词，并非亲属。

items.example: The brand was cut into every crate.
items.exampleCN: 每个木箱上都刻着那个记号。

items.example: Few buyers were aware of the second brand.
items.exampleCN: 很少有买家知道第二个品牌。

items.example: The suffix turns an adjective into a state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成一种状态。

items.example: Awareness of the recall spread quickly.
items.exampleCN: 召回的消息很快为人所知。

items.example: Half the buyers were unaware of the offer.
items.exampleCN: 一半买家不知道有这个优惠。

items.meaning: how widely a brand is known
items.example: Brand awareness doubled in a year.
items.exampleCN: 品牌知名度一年内翻倍。

items.example: Recognition needs only a glance at the label.
items.exampleCN: 认出只需瞥一眼标签。

items.meaning: bringing a name back to mind
items.example: Recall is harder than recognition.
items.exampleCN: 回想比识别更难。

definition_zh: 技术进步；技术能力、工具与工艺水平的提升
definition_en: the improvement of tools, machines, methods or technical knowledge over time
core_image: 同一块田里，牛犁、拖拉机与巡田无人机依次出现，每一代都在同一片土上留下更深的痕迹
scene: 同一块田里，先是用牛拉犁，后来用拖拉机，如今用无人机巡田。 Technological advancement has changed what a single farmer can do in a day.
sceneCN: 这里 technological advancement 指「工具与工艺水平的整体提升」（第 1 个义项：技术能力随时间的进步）；句意为技术进步改变了一个农民一天能完成的工作。可辨识物件：牛犁、拖拉机、无人机、田垄、传感器。

pos.zh: 技术进步（常作不可数）
一项技术进展（可数）

senses.title: General improvement of technique
senses.definition: the broad improvement of tools, methods and technical knowledge over time
senses.definitionCN: 工具、方法与技术知识随时间的广泛改进
senses.example: Technological advancement has changed what a single farmer can do in a day.
senses.exampleCN: 技术进步改变了一个农民一天能完成的工作。
senses.why: Advancement is forward movement, and technology is organised craft; together they name a society's growing capacity to do things.
senses.whyCN: advancement 是向前移动，technology 是组织化的技艺；合起来指一个社会做事能力的增长。

senses.title: A single breakthrough
senses.definition: one major new device or method that opens new possibilities
senses.definitionCN: 一项开辟新可能的重大新装置或方法
senses.example: The vaccine was hailed as a technological advancement of the decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疫苗被誉为这十年的一项技术突破。
senses.why: The phrase can count individual breakthroughs, not only a long trend, because progress often arrives in steps.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语可以数出单项突破，而不只是长期趋势，因为进步常以台阶形式到来。

senses.title: Productivity gains
senses.definition: the ability to produce more or better output with the same effort
senses.definitionCN: 以同样投入产出更多或更好的能力
senses.example: Technological advancement in weaving cut the cost of cloth for ordinary households.
senses.exampleCN: 织造技术的进步降低了普通家庭的布料成本。
senses.why: The economic face of the phrase is productivity: new tools change how much one hour of work can make.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语的经济面是生产率：新工具改变一小时劳动能造出多少东西。

senses.title: Social change driven by technology
senses.definition: changes in work, communication and daily life that follow new technology
senses.definitionCN: 随新技术而来的工作、通信与日常生活变化
senses.example: Technological advancement reshaped where people could work and whom they could reach.
senses.exampleCN: 技术进步重塑了人们能在哪里工作、能联系到谁。
senses.why: Tools do not stay in the workshop; they rearrange schedules, cities and families.
senses.whyCN: 工具不会留在工坊里；它们重排时间表、城市与家庭。

senses.title: The digital and information leap
senses.definition: the rapid gain in computing, storage and communication capacity
senses.definitionCN: 计算、存储与通信能力的快速提升
senses.example: Technological advancement in chips made a phone more powerful than an old room of computers.
senses.exampleCN: 芯片技术的进步让一部手机比过去一屋子电脑更强。
senses.why: The modern sense is often narrowed to digital gains, because computing has been the fastest-moving frontier.
senses.whyCN: 现代义常被收窄到数字领域的增益，因为计算是最快移动的前沿。

senses.title: Medical and life-science progress
senses.titleCN: 医学与生命科学的进步
senses.definition: new tools for diagnosis, treatment and the understanding of life
senses.definitionCN: 用于诊断、治疗与理解生命的新工具
senses.example: Technological advancement in imaging let doctors see what surgery once had to reveal.
senses.exampleCN: 成像技术的进步让医生看见过去只能靠手术揭示的东西。
senses.why: Where the object is the body, advancement is measured in survival and comfort, not only speed.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是身体时，进步以存活与舒适衡量，而不只是速度。

senses.title: Military and engineering progress
senses.titleCN: 军事与工程技术的进步
senses.definition: gains in materials, propulsion, construction and systems of control
senses.definitionCN: 材料、推进、建造与控制系统的增益
senses.example: Technological advancement in materials made the bridge both lighter and stronger.
senses.exampleCN: 材料技术的进步让这座桥更轻也更坚固。
senses.why: Engineering and warfare have often driven technique forward, because both reward precision and power.
senses.whyCN: 工程与战争常推动技艺前进，因为两者都奖赏精确与力量。

senses.title: Costs and unequal gains
senses.definition: the displacement, inequality and risk that can accompany technical progress
senses.definitionCN: 技术进展可能伴随的取代、不平等与风险
senses.example: Critics ask who bears the costs of technological advancement and who collects its gains.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者追问谁承担技术进步的代价，谁收取它的收益。
senses.why: The phrase is usually positive, but the same tools that raise output can put people out of work, so the sense carries a shadow.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语通常带正面色彩，但提高产出的同一批工具也可能让人失业，因此这一义项带着阴影。

intro.en: Technological joins Greek tekhnē 'art, craft, skill' with -logia 'study', and advancement joins advance, from Old French avancier and Vulgar Latin abantiare, with the noun suffix -ment. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: technological 由希腊 tekhnē「技艺、手艺」加表示「学问」的后缀构成；advancement 由 advance 加名词后缀构成，advance 经古法语 avancier 来自俗拉丁 abantiare。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tekhnē meant 'art, craft, skill, a systematic way of making'. Its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: tekhnē 意为「技艺、手艺、技能、系统的制作方式」。其更深来源未得到证明。

items.en: Logia meant 'study, discourse' and came from logos 'word, reason'; the compound tekhnologia named a systematic treatment of an art.
items.cn: logia 意为「学问、论述」，来自 logos「言词、理性」；合成词 tekhnologia 指对某门技艺的系统论述。

items.en: English technology appeared in the seventeenth century as a term for the systematic study of arts, and later shifted to the tools themselves.
items.cn: 英语 technology 在十七世纪出现，指对技艺的系统研究，后转指工具本身。

items.en: Advance came through Old French from Vulgar Latin abantiare, built on Latin abante 'from before', from ab 'from' and ante 'before'.
items.cn: advance 经古法语来自俗拉丁 abantiare，源于拉丁 abante「从前方」，由 ab「从」与 ante「前」构成。

items.en: The noun advancement appeared in the fourteenth century, naming a moving forward and then a improvement in rank or knowledge.
items.cn: 名词 advancement 在十四世纪出现，先指向前移动，后指地位或知识的提升。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first use of the combined phrase is not fixed, and the deeper origin of tekhnē is unsettled, so any older form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个组合短语的最早书证无法确定；tekhnē 的更早来源亦无定论，凡更早形态均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one shares the two stems; group two names progress in other registers.
note.cn: 第一组共享两个词干；第二组是用其他语域表达进步的说法。

entries.definition: The tools and systems themselves; the phrase names their improvement.
entries.definitionCN: 指工具与系统本身；短语指它们的改进。

entries.definition: Relating to technique or machinery, often in contrast to human or artistic matters.
entries.definitionCN: 与技巧或机械相关，常与人或艺术事务相对。

entries.definition: A specific way of doing something; advancement is the gain across many techniques.
entries.definitionCN: 指做某事的具体方法；进步则指许多技巧的整体增益。

entries.definition: Means by means of technology; it does not name progress.
entries.definitionCN: 意为在技术上；不指进步本身。

entries.definition: A broad word for improvement in any field; it does not specify tools.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何领域的改善，不特指工具。

entries.definition: The introduction of new products or methods; one engine of technological advancement.
entries.definitionCN: 指新产品或新方法的引入，是技术进步的一台引擎。

entries.definition: A single decisive advance that removes an obstacle.
entries.definitionCN: 指一次决定性的进展，消除了障碍。

entries.definition: A wider social process that includes technology but also institutions and habits.
entries.definitionCN: 指更广的社会过程，包含技术，也包含制度与习惯。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real contrasts, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实对比，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Greek word for craft plus the Greek word for study gives the technology half; the Latin word for forward gives the advancement half.
normal.cn: 「技艺」加「学问」组成技术这一半；「向前」加名词后缀组成进步这一半。

normal.en: The family runs technology, technological, technologically, advance, advanced, advancement.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 technology、technological、technologically、advance、advanced、advancement。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: rapid technological advancement, the pace of technological advancement.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：迅速的技术进步、技术进步的速度。

normal.en: The phrase can be uncountable for a trend or countable for a single breakthrough.
normal.cn: 这个短语可不可数指趋势，也可可数指单项突破。

normal.en: Remember the cost side: the same tools can raise output and displace workers.
normal.cn: 记住代价面：同一批工具既能提高产出，也能取代工人。

abstract.en: Picture a field where a plough, a tractor and a drone appear in turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田里依次出现犁、拖拉机与无人机。

abstract.en: Picture a phone doing the work of a room full of old machines.
abstract.cn: 想象一部手机干完一屋子旧机器的活。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge that grows lighter as its metal grows stronger.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥随金属变强而变轻。

examples.en: Technological advancement lowered the cost of solar power faster than forecasts expected.
examples.cn: 技术进步使太阳能成本下降得比预测更快。

examples.en: The report links technological advancement to wage gaps rather than to overall growth alone.
examples.cn: 报告把技术进步与工资差距联系起来，而非只看总体增长。

examples.en: Each technological advancement in printing made books cheaper to own.
examples.cn: 印刷术的每一次技术进步都让书籍更便宜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「technological（技术的）+ advancement（前进）」——工具一代代往前走，把人的手越伸越长

root: technological 来自希腊 tekhnē「技艺」与表示「学问」的后缀；advancement 来自 advance 加名词后缀，advance 经古法语 avancier 出自俗拉丁 abantiare，源于拉丁 abante（ab + ante，从前方）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one rising line: technique improves overall, a breakthrough opens a door, output rises, society rearranges, computing leaps, medicine and engineering gain, and the costs appear.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条上升线展开：技艺整体提高，一项突破打开一扇门，产出上升，社会重新排布，计算能力跃迁，医学与工程获益，代价也随之出现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same field crossed first by a plough, then a tractor, then a drone.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一块田先被犁走过，再被拖拉机走过，最后被无人机掠过。

branches.en: THE TREND: improvement is continuous and cumulative.
branches.cn: 趋势：改进是连续且累积的。

branches.en: STEPS AND SYSTEMS: a single breakthrough and a whole engineering field both move the line.
branches.cn: 台阶与系统：单项突破与整个工程领域都在推动这条线。

branches.en: OUTPUT AND LIFE: productivity changes work, and work rearranges society.
branches.cn: 产出与生活：生产率改变工作，工作又重排社会。

branches.en: COMPUTING AND BODY: chips and medicine are the two most visible frontiers.
branches.cn: 计算与身体：芯片与医学是最可见的两个前沿。

branches.en: THE SHADOW: every gain has a bearer of cost.
branches.cn: 阴影：每一项收益都有承担代价的人。

intro.en: The phrase can be read from a Greek noun for craft, a Greek noun for study, and a Latin-derived verb of moving forward.
intro.cn: 这个短语可以按表示技艺的希腊名词、表示学问的希腊名词，以及拉丁来源的「向前移动」动词读出。

latinIntro.en: Greek tekhnē supplies technology and technique; Greek logos supplies the study suffix; Latin abante supplies advance and advancement.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 tekhnē 衍生 technology 与 technique；希腊 logos 提供表示学问的后缀；拉丁 abante 衍生 advance 与 advancement。

items.example: The noun supplies the craft half of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供词中「技艺」的一半。

items.example: The suffix names a field of study.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀指一个研究领域。

items.meaning: the study of arts; later tools and systems
items.meaningCN: 技艺研究；后指工具与系统
items.example: Technology shifted from study to hardware.
items.exampleCN: technology 从研究转向硬件。

items.example: Technological change is fast.
items.exampleCN: 技术变化很快。

items.example: A technique is one method.
items.exampleCN: 技巧是一种方法。

items.example: The preposition begins the Latin phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个介词开启拉丁短语。

items.example: The word names what stands before.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指在前之物。

items.example: The adverb gave the verb of moving forward.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词衍生出向前移动的动词。

items.example: Tools advance year by year.
items.exampleCN: 工具逐年推进。

items.example: Advancement can be measured.
items.exampleCN: 进步可以被衡量。

definition_zh: 重叠；部分覆盖同一区域；时间上部分重合；范围或职责部分相同；重叠部分；重叠量
definition_en: to cover part of the same surface, period, or range as something else, or to share part of it; also the shared part itself and its extent
core_image: 两张半透明胶片错开叠放，中间交叠的那一带颜色明显变深
scene: 调度员把白班和夜班的排班表铺在桌上。 The two shifts overlap for one hour between seven and eight, and that hour is marked in dark ink.
sceneCN: 这里 overlap 是「时间上部分重合」（第 2 个义项：共用一段时间）；句意：两个班次在七点到八点之间重叠一小时，那一小时被涂成深色。图中可辨识物件：两张排班表、荧光笔、深色的一小时格子、值班帽。

pos.zh: 部分覆盖同一区域；交叠
（时间）部分重合；与……同时发生一段
（范围、兴趣、职责）部分相同；有交集
重叠部分；交叠区域
重叠量；重合程度

derivatives.zh: 已交叠的；被覆盖住一部分的

senses.title: Cover the same surface
senses.definition: to cover part of the same area of a surface as another thing
senses.definitionCN: 与另一物覆盖同一块表面的一部分
senses.example: The two labels overlap slightly at the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 两张标签在角上略微重叠。
senses.why: Over- here means across or above, and lap means to fold or lay one thing over another. A layer laid across the edge of another shares a strip of surface with it, and that strip is the overlap.
senses.whyCN: over- 在这里是“越过、在上”，lap 是“折叠、把一层搭到另一层上”。一层越过另一层的边缘搭上去，两者就共用一条表面，这条共用的带子就是重叠。

senses.title: Share part of the same period
senses.definition: to happen during part of the same period as something else
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事发生在同一段时间的一部分
senses.example: My lecture overlaps with the lab session on Thursday.
senses.exampleCN: 周四我的讲座和实验课时间重叠。
senses.why: When layers become schedules, the shared strip becomes shared minutes. The geometry is unchanged: two stretches laid along one line share a middle segment.
senses.whyCN: 当“层”变成“日程”，共用的那条带子就变成了共用的分钟。几何关系没有变：两条线段铺在同一条时间线上，中间有一段是双方都占着的。

senses.title: Share part of a range
senses.definition: to share part of a range of values, topics, or interests
senses.definitionCN: 在一段数值、话题或兴趣范围中有一部分相同
senses.example: Their research interests overlap in cognitive science.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的研究兴趣在认知科学上重叠。
senses.why: A range is a line with limits. Two ranges that share a stretch of that line overlap exactly as two strips share a band of surface, which is why the same word serves for both.
senses.whyCN: 范围是一条有端点的时间轴或数轴。两段范围共用其中一截，就像两条带子共用一段表面一样，因此同一个词可以同时用于空间、时间和抽象范围。

senses.title: Share duties: jobs that claim the same tasks
senses.titleCN: 职责重叠：两个岗位claim同一批任务
senses.definition: of jobs or responsibilities, to include the same tasks or territory
senses.definitionCN: 指岗位或职责包含同一批任务、同一片权责范围
senses.example: The two roles overlap, so one person could cover both.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个岗位职责重叠，一个人就能兼顾。
senses.why: Duties are territories drawn around tasks. When two job descriptions claim the same task, their territories share a zone; managers then redraw the boundaries to remove the overlap.
senses.whyCN: 职责是围绕任务划出的地盘。两份岗位说明都声称管同一件事时，它们的地盘就出现共用区；管理者随后要重划边界，消掉这块重叠。

senses.title: The shared part itself
senses.definition: the area, period, or set of items that two things both include
senses.definitionCN: 两个事物同时包含的区域、时段或项目集合
senses.example: The overlap between the two plans is small.
senses.exampleCN: 两个计划之间重叠的部分很小。
senses.why: English often turns the place where two things meet into a noun. The verb describes the laying across; the noun names the strip that results, as if you could point at it on a map.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把“两物相接之处”直接名词化。动词描述“搭过去”的动作，名词则指动作留下的那条带子，仿佛能在地图上指出来。

senses.title: How much is shared: measured overlap
senses.titleCN: 重叠量：被度量的重合程度
senses.definition: the extent to which two things cover the same ground, often given as a proportion
senses.definitionCN: 两个事物覆盖同一范围的程度，常以比例表示
senses.example: There is a 30 percent overlap between the two datasets.
senses.exampleCN: 两个数据集有百分之三十的重叠。
senses.why: Once the shared zone can be pointed at, it can be measured. Statistics and design turn the strip into a number, so overlap becomes a degree rather than a place.
senses.whyCN: 共用区一旦能被指出来，就能被测量。统计学与设计把这条带子变成一个数字，于是重叠从“一个地方”变成了“一个程度”。

senses.title: Printing and imaging: lay one layer over another
senses.titleCN: 印刷与影像：一层压在一层上
senses.definition: in printing and image editing, to place or print one layer partly over another
senses.definitionCN: 在印刷与图像编辑中，把一层部分地压在另一层上
senses.example: The poster overlaps the photo with a red block.
senses.exampleCN: 海报用一个红色色块压住了照片的一部分。
senses.why: This is the craft sense at its most literal: ink or film laid across the edge of another layer. Where the two layers meet, the colours combine and the shared band darkens, which is exactly the image behind the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最字面的手艺义：油墨或胶片越过另一层的边缘压上去。两层相接处颜色叠加、共用带变深，正是这个词背后的原始画面。

senses.title: Handover overlap: both present for a while
senses.titleCN: 交接重叠期：两任同时在岗
senses.definition: a period when the outgoing and incoming person are both at work so that knowledge can pass between them
senses.definitionCN: 离任者与接任者同时在岗的一段时间，以便经验传递
senses.example: The new manager had a two-week overlap with her predecessor.
senses.exampleCN: 新经理与前任有两周的重叠期。
senses.why: In time, the shared strip can be deliberately arranged. It is the only window in which tacit knowledge can be shown rather than written down, so organizations schedule an overlap instead of a clean cut.
senses.whyCN: 在时间上，这条共用带子可以被刻意安排出来。它是默会知识能够“演示”而不是“写成文件”的唯一窗口，所以组织会安排一段重叠，而不是一刀切地换人。

intro.en: Overlap is a native English compound of two old words. The dates are recorded first uses, and the deeper origin of lap is not certain.
intro.cn: overlap 是两个古老英语本族词构成的复合词。年代为首次记录时间；lap 的更早来源并不确定。

items.en: The phrase lap over is recorded meaning 'to lie partly on or over something'. The image is a cloth or board laid across the edge of another.
items.cn: 短语 lap over 记录于 17 世纪 30 年代，意为“部分地搭在某物之上”。画面是一块布或木板越过另一物的边缘搭上去。

items.en: The single verb overlap appears, meaning 'to lay so as to cover part of something else'. It is formed by reversing the phrase: over + lap.
items.cn: 合为一体的动词 overlap 出现于 1726 年，意为“铺盖住另一物的一部分”。它由短语的词序调转而来：over + lap。

items.en: The noun overlap is recorded, first as the act of overlapping and then as the part that is shared.
items.cn: 名词 overlap 记录于 1813 年，先指“重叠这个动作”，后指“被共用的那部分”。

items.en: Technical use spreads: overlapping boards in shipbuilding, overlapping strata in geology, overlapping genes in genetics, and overlapping segments in phonology.
items.cn: 技术用法扩散开来：造船中的搭接板、地质学中的重叠地层、遗传学中的重叠基因、音系学中的重叠音段。

items.en: The figurative senses dominate now: overlapping interests, overlapping duties, and a scheduled overlap between two job holders. The physical strip remains the model for all of them.
items.cn: 如今占主导的是引申义：兴趣重叠、职责重叠、两任岗位之间的交接重叠期。那条物理上的共用带子仍是所有用法的模型。

note.en: The first group is about shape: over- words that do not mean sharing a zone. The second is about meaning: words for things that meet, cross, or repeat.
note.cn: 第一组看外形：同样带 over- 却不表示“共用一块区域”的词。第二组看词义：表示相接、相交或重复的词。

entries.definition: to lie over or on top of something, especially in layers of rock. It stresses one layer covering another, not a shared strip.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖在……之上，尤指岩层。它强调一层盖住另一层，而不是共用一条带子。

entries.definition: to cover the surface of something with a layer, or the layer itself. The covering can be complete, while overlap is only partial.
entries.definitionCN: 在某物表面覆上一层，或指那一层本身。覆盖可以是完全的，而 overlap 只是部分的。

entries.definition: to load too much, or an excessive load. It shares the over- prefix but has nothing to do with shared area.
entries.definitionCN: 超载；装载过多。它同样带 over-，但与“共用区域”无关。

entries.definition: to look down on something from above, or to fail to notice it. Its over- is about position or neglect, not coverage.
entries.definitionCN: 俯瞰；忽视。它的 over- 表示位置或忽略，而不是覆盖。

entries.definition: to happen at the same time or occupy the same space exactly. It stresses simultaneous or identical position; overlap stresses a shared part.
entries.definitionCN: 同时发生，或完全占据同一空间。它强调同时或位置完全一致；overlap 强调“共有一部分”。

entries.definition: to cross or cut through each other, or to share common elements in set theory. Crossing produces a line or point; overlapping produces an area.
entries.definitionCN: 相交、交叉，或在集合论中有共同元素。交叉产生的是线或点，重叠产生的是面积。

entries.definition: to make an exact copy, or an exact copy itself. Complete sameness is the point, whereas overlap allows each side to keep something of its own.
entries.definitionCN: 复制；完全相同的副本。重点在“完全一样”，而重叠允许双方各自保留一部分。

entries.definition: to place one image or layer on top of another so that both remain visible. It is the technical cousin of the printing sense of overlap.
entries.definitionCN: 把一个影像或一层叠在另一层上，且两者都仍然可见。它是 overlap 印刷义的技术近亲。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks built on sound and spelling, then three abstract images for the idea of a shared strip.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个读音与拼写挂钩，再用三个抽象画面记住“共用一条带子”这个观念。

normal.en: lap is the knee: a book lies across your lap. Over-lap is one thing lying across another, sharing a strip.
normal.cn: lap 是“膝上”：书横放在膝上。over-lap 就是一物横搭在另一物上，共用一条带子。

normal.en: The verb is stressed at the back, the noun at the front: overLAP the sheets, but close the OVERlap. The heavier stress marks the action.
normal.cn: 动词重音在后，名词重音在前：overLAP 两张纸，但收拢 OVERlap。重音落在动作上。

normal.en: Hear the hyphen: over-lap means crossing the edge and lapping onto the other side.
normal.cn: 想象那个连字符：over-lap 就是越过边缘、搭到另一侧去。

normal.en: Picture a Venn diagram: the dark lens in the middle is the overlap, and both circles can point at it.
normal.cn: 想一个维恩图：中间那块深色透镜就是重叠部分，两个圆都能指向它。

normal.en: Shift change at a factory: the ten minutes when both crews are on the floor is the overlap.
normal.cn: 工厂交接班：两个班组同时站在车间里的那十分钟，就是 overlap。

abstract.en: Overlap is not similarity. It is a real shared interval that both sides can occupy at once.
abstract.cn: 重叠不是“相似”。它是一段双方都能同时占用的真实共用区间。

abstract.en: Cooperation starts in the overlap: the small zone of shared interest is the only ground on which two plans can be signed.
abstract.cn: 合作从重叠处开始：那一小块共同利益，是两个计划唯一能签字的地面。

abstract.en: Shared time is the one resource that cannot be returned. If two things overlap, they must be carried together.
abstract.cn: 共用的时间是无法退还的资源。两件事一旦重叠，就只能一起承担。

examples.en: The two circles overlap, and the shaded lens is where both claims hold.
examples.cn: 两个圆重叠，阴影的透镜形区域就是两种主张都成立的地方。

examples.en: Her new job overlaps with the old one for a month, which is enough time to hand over the files.
examples.cn: 她的新工作与旧工作有一个月的重叠期，足够交接文件。

examples.en: When the duties of two departments overlap, someone has to decide who answers the phone.
examples.cn: 当两个部门的职责重叠时，总得有人决定谁来接电话。

dict_mnemonic.note: 把 over 记成“越过、在上”，lap 记成“搭、叠”：越过边界搭上一块，就是重叠。
dict_mnemonic.text: over（越过、在上）+ lap（搭叠）→ 部分重叠；重叠部分、重叠量

root: over（在上、越过）+ lap（搭、折叠）；lap 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The senses start with two surfaces sharing a strip, move the same strip through time and then through abstract ranges and duties, then name the strip and measure it, and end with the two technical uses where the strip is deliberate: printing layers and a job handover.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从“两块表面共用一条带子”开始，把同一条带子依次移到时间、抽象范围与职责上，再把它名词化并加以度量，最后落到两种刻意安排的带子：印刷叠层与岗位交接。

core.en: Two sheets laid across each other, leaving one darker shared band
core.cn: 两张错开叠放的薄片，留下一条颜色更深的共用带

branches.en: Physical sharing: two surfaces cover the same patch.
branches.cn: 物理共用：两块表面覆盖同一片区域。

branches.en: Time sharing: an accidental clash of schedules, or a deliberate handover window.
branches.cn: 时间共用：日程的意外相撞，或刻意留出的交接窗口。

branches.en: Abstract sharing: interests that meet, and duties that claim the same task.
branches.cn: 抽象共用：相交的兴趣，以及争夺同一任务的两份职责。

branches.en: The strip named, then the strip measured as a proportion.
branches.cn: 先给这条带子命名，再把它度量成一个比例。

branches.en: Literal layering: ink or film pressed across another layer, darkening the shared band.
branches.cn: 字面叠层：油墨或胶片压过另一层，使共用带变深。

intro.en: Overlap sits in the huge over- family and the small lap family. Both halves are native English, so there is no Latin root here.
intro.cn: overlap 属于庞大的 over- 词族，也属于小小的 lap 词族。两半都是英语本族词，因此这里没有拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entry applies: over is Old English ofer, from Proto-Germanic *uber (PIE *uper); lap is a Germanic verb of uncertain deeper origin.
latinIntro.cn: 不适用拉丁词条：over 是古英语 ofer，来自原始日耳曼语 *uber（原始印欧语 *uper）；lap 是一个日耳曼语动词，其更早来源不确定。

items.meaning: to cover part of the same area, time, or range
items.meaningCN: 部分覆盖同一区域、时段或范围
items.example: The two schedules overlap on Friday.
items.exampleCN: 两份日程在周五重叠。

items.structure: same compound used as a noun
items.meaning: the shared part; the extent of sharing
items.example: The overlap is only ten percent.
items.exampleCN: 重叠部分只有百分之十。

items.meaning: sharing part of the same area or range
items.example: The two overlapping claims caused a dispute.
items.exampleCN: 两项重叠的主张引发了争议。

items.meaningCN: 被部分覆盖的；交叠起来的
items.example: The overlapped boards kept the rain out.
items.exampleCN: 交叠搭接的木板挡住了雨。

items.meaning: sharing no area or range at all
items.example: The two groups are nonoverlapping.
items.exampleCN: 这两个群体完全没有重叠。

items.meaning: across, above, beyond, or too much
items.example: Overhead, overland, overcharge.
items.exampleCN: 头顶的、陆路的、多收钱。

items.meaning: to fold or lay one thing over another
items.meaningCN: 折叠；把一物搭在另一物上
items.example: Lap the edge of the cloth over the seam.
items.exampleCN: 把布边搭过接缝。

items.meaning: a joint where one part falls short of covering another
items.meaningCN: 下搭接；欠重叠（工程中相接不足的接缝）
items.example: The engineer measured the underlap of the plates.
items.exampleCN: 工程师测量了钢板的欠重叠量。

items.meaning: in a way that shares part of the same area or range
items.example: The two terms are used overlappingly in the literature.
items.exampleCN: 文献中这两个术语被重叠地使用。

definition_zh: 铁器时代：以铁器的使用为主要技术标志的考古时期，通常位于青铜时代之后；也指某一地区的这一阶段
definition_en: the archaeological period marked by the use of iron, usually following the Bronze Age, and the regional stage of that period
core_image: 展柜里锈迹斑斑的铁剑与犁头排成一列，说明牌只给出一段年代
scene: 展柜里锈迹斑斑的铁剑与犁头排成一列，旁边的说明牌只写着一个年代区间。 The Iron Age is dated from the first widespread smelting of iron.
sceneCN: 这里指作为考古分期的铁器时代（第 1 个义项：以铁器为标志的时期名）；句意为铁器时代的起点，是以铁的普遍熔炼来断代的。

pos.zh: 铁器时代（专有名词，考古分期）
某一地区的铁器时代阶段
铁器时代的（作定语，常写作 Iron-Age 或 iron-age）

collocations.phrase: the end of the Iron Age

forms.label: 相关称法（无铁器阶段的地区）

derivatives.zh: iron（铁）+ age（时代）中的材料基础 → 金属本身；时代名由材料名加「时代」构成
iron age + 连字符作定语 → 铁器时代的，语义偏移为「属于该期风格或技术的」
小写连字符形式 → 铁器时代的（多见于英式行文）
iron age + man → 铁器时代的人，语义偏移为「该期人群的泛称」

senses.title: The named period
senses.titleCN: 时期名：以铁器为标志的阶段
senses.definition: the period of human culture marked by the use of iron, usually placed after the Bronze Age
senses.definitionCN: 以使用铁器为标志、通常排在青铜时代之后的人类文化时期
senses.example: The Iron Age is dated from the first widespread smelting of iron.
senses.exampleCN: 铁器时代的起点，是以铁的普遍熔炼来断代的。
senses.why: The name comes from a scheme that sorts societies by their dominant metal; iron is the material that follows bronze in that sequence.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字来自一种按主导金属给社会分期的方案；在这一序列里，铁是排在青铜之后的材料。

senses.title: A region's version
senses.titleCN: 地区性阶段：某一地区的铁器时代
senses.definition: the local stretch of time in which a particular region used iron as its main metal
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区以铁为主要金属的那一段本地时间
senses.example: The Iron Age in this region began with the first local smelting of iron.
senses.exampleCN: 这一地区的铁器时代，始于本地第一次炼铁。
senses.why: Iron reached different regions at different times and sometimes not at all, so the label is always tied to a place rather than to a single date.
senses.whyCN: 铁到达各地区的时间不同，有些地区甚至没有经历这一阶段，因此这个标签总是与地点绑定，而不是与单一日期绑定。

senses.title: The society of the period
senses.definition: the people, settlements and way of life of that period taken as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体来看的该时期人群、聚落与生活方式
senses.example: Iron Age society here was organised around fortified hilltops.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的铁器时代社会围绕设防的山顶组织起来。
senses.why: A period name can stand for the life inside it, especially when the new metal changed farming, warfare and trade together.
senses.whyCN: 时期名可以代替该时期内生活本身，尤其当这种新金属同时改变了农耕、战争与贸易时。

senses.title: The attributive use
senses.titleCN: 定语用法：铁器时代的器物与遗址
senses.definition: used before a noun to mark an object, site or practice as belonging to that period
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，标明某器物、遗址或做法属于该时期
senses.example: Iron Age weapons were often repaired rather than replaced.
senses.exampleCN: 铁器时代的武器常常是修补而不是替换。
senses.why: English lets a period name modify a noun directly, so one phrase can turn a blade, a ditch or a farm into a dated thing.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许时期名直接修饰名词，于是一个短语就能把一把刀、一道沟或一处农庄变成有年代归属的东西。

senses.title: Iron after bronze
senses.titleCN: 在分期中的位置：铁取代青铜成为主材
senses.definition: the stage in the three-age system that follows the Bronze Age and precedes no further metal stage
senses.definitionCN: 三段体系中排在青铜时代之后、且不再有后续金属阶段的那一级
senses.example: Iron displaced bronze first for tools, later for weapons.
senses.exampleCN: 铁先在工具上取代青铜，之后才在武器上取代。
senses.why: The ladder ends here: iron ore is widespread and iron can be made harder than bronze, so the sequence has no fourth rung based on a common metal.
senses.whyCN: 阶梯到这里为止：铁矿分布广，铁又能做得比青铜更硬，因此这个序列没有以常见金属为基础的第四级。

senses.title: Early, middle and late
senses.titleCN: 早中晚三段：更细的分期
senses.definition: a subdivision of the period into early, middle and late phases, where the local sequence allows it
senses.definitionCN: 在本地序列允许时，把该时期细分为早期、中期与晚期
senses.example: The Late Iron Age saw larger and better-made iron bars.
senses.exampleCN: 铁器时代晚期出现了更大、更精良的铁条。
senses.why: A long period needs internal divisions to be usable, and the standard early, middle and late labels are added in front of the same name.
senses.whyCN: 一段长时期需要内部划分才好用，于是标准的早、中、晚标签被加在同一个名字前面。

senses.title: Evidence and dating
senses.titleCN: 证据与断代：凭什么判断这一时期
senses.definition: the material evidence, such as slag, furnace remains and iron objects, used to date and define the period
senses.definitionCN: 用来判定与界定该时期的有形证据，如炉渣、炉址与铁器
senses.example: Slag heaps and furnace bottoms are the best Iron Age evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 炉渣堆与炉底是判定铁器时代最好的证据。
senses.why: A period named after an industry is dated by that industry's waste: furnaces and slag survive when individual tools are reworked or rusted away.
senses.whyCN: 以某个行业命名的时期，要靠该行业的废弃物来断代：炉子与炉渣能留存，而单件工具往往被改锻或锈蚀殆尽。

senses.title: An old stage, in speech
senses.titleCN: 口语比喻：过时、老旧的阶段
senses.definition: used informally for an outdated stage of technology or practice
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法，指技术或做法上已经过时的阶段
senses.example: Their ticketing belongs to the iron age of computing.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的售票系统还停留在计算机的铁器时代。
senses.why: Once a period name means 'early and superseded', it can be borrowed for anything old-fashioned; iron, though later than bronze, still sounds primitive next to modern materials.
senses.whyCN: 一旦时期名意味着「早期且已被取代」，它就能借来形容任何过时之物；铁虽晚于青铜，但与现代材料相比仍显得原始。

intro.en: The phrase joins an ancient Germanic metal name to a period word from Latin, and its modern sense belongs to the nineteenth-century classification of prehistory by materials.
intro.cn: 这个短语把古老的日耳曼金属名与来自拉丁的时期词接在一起，现代义属于十九世纪按材料划分史前的分类法。

items.en: Old English isern and iren named the metal. The deeper origin is debated: a early Celtic loan is often suggested but not proven, and every Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 古英语 isern 与 iren 指这种金属。更早来源有争议：常有人猜测是早期凯尔特语借词，但未获证明，凡为它拟出的印欧形式都是重构。

items.en: Age came through Old French from Latin aetas, meaning a lifetime or a span of time, before it was used for a division of history.
items.cn: age 经古法语来自拉丁 aetas，本义是一生或一段时间，之后才被用于历史分期。

items.en: Stone, Bronze and Iron were established as a sequence by Christian Jürgensen Thomsen in the 1830s, using the materials of museum finds as the sorting principle.
items.cn: 石、青铜、铁这一序列，由汤姆森在十九世纪三十年代确立，以博物馆藏品的材料作为分类原则。

items.en: English adopted Iron Age in the middle of the nineteenth century with the rest of the three-age vocabulary, first for European and Mediterranean sequences.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪中叶与三段分期的其余词汇一同采纳 Iron Age，最先用于欧洲与地中海的年代序列。

items.en: Twentieth-century archaeology added early, middle and late phases, recognised regions with no Iron Age at all, and let the phrase serve as an attributive label.
items.cn: 二十世纪考古学加入了早、中、晚三段，承认有些地区根本没有铁器时代，并让这个短语充当定语标签。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English citation is not fixed, the origin of the metal word is unsettled, and the period's dates vary by centuries from region to region.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语首见书证没有定论，金属词的来源未解决，而该时期年代在不同地区相差数百年。

note.en: Group one separates the phrase from its shorter forms and related labels; group two separates it from the other periods in the same scheme.
note.cn: 第一组把这个短语与它的短形式及相关标签分开；第二组把它与同一体系中的其他时期分开。

entries.definition: The metal itself. The phrase names a period; the bare noun names the substance and the objects made from it.
entries.definitionCN: 金属本身。这个短语命名一个时期，而单独的名词命名物质及其器物。

entries.definition: The same phrase with a hyphen when it stands before a noun; the hyphen marks its adjectival job.
entries.definitionCN: 同一短语在名词前作定语时加连字符；连字符标出它作形容词的角色。

entries.definition: A name for sharp social breakdown at the end of some regional Iron Ages; it is an episode, not the period.
entries.definitionCN: 指某些地区铁器时代末期社会急剧崩溃的说法；它是一个事件，而不是整个时期。

entries.definition: Iron with added carbon, harder and more elastic; steel is a product of iron, not a period name.
entries.definitionCN: 加入碳的铁，更硬更有弹性；钢是铁的产物，不是时期名。

entries.definition: The preceding period in the same three-age scheme, marked by bronze.
entries.definitionCN: 同一三段体系中更早的时期，以青铜为标志。

entries.definition: The earliest period in the same scheme, marked by stone tools.
entries.definitionCN: 同一体系中最早的时期，以石器为标志。

entries.definition: A transitional stage of copper working alongside stone, often inserted between the Stone and Bronze Ages.
entries.definitionCN: 铜与石器并用的过渡阶段，常被插在石器时代与青铜时代之间。

entries.definition: Any dated division of the past defined by material or culture; the Iron Age is one such division.
entries.definitionCN: 按材料或文化划定的任何有年代的过去片段；铁器时代只是其中一个划分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the metal name, its place in the ladder, and the real regional caveat.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：金属名、它在阶梯上的位置，以及真实的地区性例外。

normal.en: The phrase is self-explaining: iron + age, a stretch of time labelled by its dominant metal.
normal.cn: 这个短语自我解释：铁 + 时代，用主导金属给一段时间贴标签。

normal.en: The ladder ends with iron: stone, bronze, iron, and no fourth common metal.
normal.cn: 阶梯到铁为止：石、青铜、铁，没有第四种常见金属。

normal.en: Regional honesty matters: some regions have no Iron Age, and the dates shift by centuries.
normal.cn: 地区差异必须如实交代：有些地区没有铁器时代，年代相差数百年。

normal.en: The evidence words are slag, furnace and ore: waste and structures outlast the tools.
normal.cn: 证据词是炉渣、炉址与矿石：废弃物与结构比工具存留更久。

normal.en: The phrase is proper as a period name and hyphenated when it modifies a noun.
normal.cn: 作时期名时首字母大写；修饰名词时加连字符。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder whose top rung is the last one made of a common metal, with nothing above it but alloy steel.
abstract.cn: 想象一道阶梯，最高一级是最后一种常见金属做成的，上面再没有东西，只剩合金钢。

abstract.en: Picture a rusted blade beside a heap of slag: the tool decays, the waste remains.
abstract.cn: 想象一把锈刀旁堆着炉渣：工具烂掉了，废弃物却留下来。

abstract.en: Picture a label that must always carry a place name, because the same word covers centuries that do not line up.
abstract.cn: 想象一张标签必须总带一个地名，因为同一个词覆盖的世纪彼此对不齐。

examples.en: The Iron Age began at different dates in different parts of the continent.
examples.cn: 铁器时代在这块大陆的不同地区始于不同年代。

examples.en: Iron Age farmers used iron-tipped ploughs on heavier soils.
examples.cn: 铁器时代的农民在较重的土壤上使用带铁尖的犁。

examples.en: The fort was rebuilt several times during the Late Iron Age.
examples.cn: 这座堡垒在铁器时代晚期多次重建。

dict_mnemonic.text: iron（铁）+ age（时代）＝ 铁器时代；记「石—青铜—铁，铁是最后一级」。

root: iron 来自古英语 īsern／īren，更早来源不确定，凯尔特语借词说未获证明；age 经古法语来自拉丁 aetas「一生、时期」。两词合成，指以铁器为标志的考古时期。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace one label: the period, its regional versions, its society, its attributive use, its place after bronze, its subdivisions, its evidence, and its joking use for anything outdated.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一个标签展开：时期本身、地区版本、该期社会、定语用法、排在青铜之后的位置、内部细分、断代证据，以及用来调侃过时之物的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rusted iron blades and plough tips in a case, beside a label that gives only a span of years.
core.cn: 核心意象：展柜里锈蚀的铁剑与犁尖，旁边标签只写着一个年代区间。

branches.en: THE LABEL: one name for the last metal stage of the three-part scheme.
branches.cn: 标签本身：三段体系中最后一个金属阶段的名称。

branches.en: THE LOCAL AND THE INTERNAL: one region's stretch of the period, and its early, middle and late phases.
branches.cn: 地方与内部：某一地区的那一段，以及它的早、中、晚三段。

branches.en: THE LIFE INSIDE: the label stands for farms, forts and the society that built them.
branches.cn: 期内生活：标签代替了农庄、堡垒以及建造它们的社会。

branches.en: THE MODIFIER: attached to weapons and settlements in the ordinary way, and borrowed in speech for anything outdated.
branches.cn: 修饰用法：正常地附着到武器与聚落上，也被口语借去形容过时之物。

branches.en: THE LADDER AND THE PROOF: the rung after bronze, held up by slag, furnace bottoms and dated iron.
branches.cn: 阶梯与证据：排在青铜之后的一级，由炉渣、炉底与可测年的铁器支撑。

intro.en: The phrase is a compound of two free words; the second carries the period sense, and a hyphen appears when the compound works as an adjective.
intro.cn: 这个短语是两个自由词构成的复合词；第二个词带时期义，作形容词时会加连字符。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the period word through aetas, but it has no cognate of the metal word; the Latin name for iron, ferrum, belongs to a different family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语通过 aetas 提供时期词，却没有与金属词同源的形式；拉丁语指铁的词 ferrum 属于另一个词族。
